definition.stemRaw:
You need to create a Power BI theme for use across multiple reports. The theme must incorporate corporate branding for font size, color, and bar chart formatting.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Power BI Desktop, customize the current theme.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Power BI Desktop, use a built-in report theme.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a theme as a PBIVIZ file and import the theme into Power BI Desktop.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a theme as a JSON file and import the theme into Power BI Desktop.

definition.explanation:
Power BI custom report themes use JSON files. The JSON theme format supports colors, text settings including font size, and visual formatting settings; importing the file into Power BI Desktop makes the standardized theme reusable across reports.

**Learn more:** [Create custom report themes in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/report-themes-create-custom) · [Use report themes in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-report-themes)

finalExplanation: Power BI custom report themes use JSON files. The JSON theme format supports colors, text settings including font size, and visual formatting settings; importing the file into Power BI Desktop makes the standardized theme reusable across reports.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI workspace called Workspace1 that contains a dataset named DS1 and a report named RPT1.  
  
A user wants to create a report using the data in DS1 and publish that report to a different workspace.  
  
You need to give the user the appropriate access while minimizing the number of permissions granted.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the user as a Viewer of Workspace1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Grant the Build permission for DS1 to the user.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Share RPT1 with the user.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the user as a member of Workspace1.

definition.explanation:
Build permission on a Power BI semantic model enables users to create new reports and other content from that model. It is required to create a report in one workspace based on a semantic model located in another workspace, without granting broader Workspace1 membership or access to an unrelated existing report.

**Learn more:** [Create reports based on semantic models from different workspaces - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-datasets-discover-across-workspaces) · [Build Permission for Shared Semantic Models - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-datasets-build-permissions)

finalExplanation: Build permission on a Power BI semantic model enables users to create new reports and other content from that model. It is required to create a report in one workspace based on a semantic model located in another workspace, without granting broader Workspace1 membership or access to an unrelated existing report.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI dashboard that monitors manufacturing-process quality. The dashboard includes the following elements:  
  
- A line chart showing the number of defective products manufactured each day  
- A KPI visual showing the current daily percentage of defective products manufactured  
  
You need to receive a notification when the daily percentage of defective products manufactured exceeds 3%.  
  
What should you create?

choices.label: A
choices.text: a subscription

choices.label: B
choices.text: an alert

choices.label: C
choices.text: a smart narrative visual

choices.label: D
choices.text: a Q&A visual

definition.explanation:
Power BI data alerts notify users when refreshed dashboard data passes a configured threshold. Alerts are supported for KPI tiles, so an alert can be configured to trigger when the daily defective-product percentage is greater than 3%.

**Learn more:** [Set data alerts in the Power BI service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-set-data-alerts)

finalExplanation: Power BI data alerts notify users when refreshed dashboard data passes a configured threshold. Alerts are supported for KPI tiles, so an alert can be configured to trigger when the daily defective-product percentage is greater than 3%.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model named Model1 that uses Import storage mode.  
  
You need to decrease the size of Model1. The solution must **NOT** increase report query response times.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove unnecessary columns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unpivot unnecessary columns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rename unnecessary columns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change Model1 to DirectQuery storage mode.

definition.explanation:
Removing unnecessary columns reduces the amount of data stored in the Import semantic model while retaining Import mode’s in-memory query performance. Unpivoting may increase row count, renaming columns does not reduce stored data, and DirectQuery can add source-query latency.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction) · [Semantic model modes in the Power BI service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-dataset-modes-understand)

finalExplanation: Removing unnecessary columns reduces the amount of data stored in the Import semantic model while retaining Import mode’s in-memory query performance. Unpivoting may increase row count, renaming columns does not reduce stored data, and DirectQuery can add source-query latency.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a report containing four pages. Each page has slicers for the same four fields.  
  
Users report that when they choose values in a slicer on one page, those selections do not persist on the other pages.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that lets users select a value once and filter results across all pages. What are two possible recommendations to meet this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a bookmark for each slicer value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the slicers with report-level filters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sync the slicers across the pages.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replace the slicers with page-level filters.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replace the slicers with visual-level filters.

definition.explanation:
Power BI Sync slicers can synchronize slicer filter selections across report pages, so a selection made on one page affects visuals on the synchronized pages. A report-level filter applies to all pages in the report, providing a single report-wide filtering scope. Page-level and visual-level filters are limited to their respective page or visual.

**Learn more:** [Slicers in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-visualization-slicers) · [Add a filter to a report in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/power-bi-report-add-filter)

finalExplanation: Power BI Sync slicers can synchronize slicer filter selections across report pages, so a selection made on one page affects visuals on the synchronized pages. A report-level filter applies to all pages in the report, providing a single report-wide filtering scope. Page-level and visual-level filters are limited to their respective page or visual.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a PBIX file that imports data from a Microsoft Excel data source located on a file share in a local network.  
  
You are informed that the Excel data source has been moved to a different location.  
  
You need to update the PBIX file so that it uses the new location.  
  
What are three ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: From the Datasets settings of the Power BI service, configure the data source credentials.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From the Data source settings in Power BI Desktop, configure the file path.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From Current File in Power BI Desktop, configure the Data Load settings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From Power Query Editor, use the formula bar to configure the file path for the applied step.

choices.label: E
choices.text: From Advanced Editor in Power Query Editor, configure the file path in the M code.

definition.explanation:
The Excel connector’s source location is part of the query’s source definition. Power BI Desktop can update that location through Data source settings, while Power Query can update the path in the Source applied step through the formula bar or directly in the query’s M code through Advanced Editor. Service credential settings control authentication, and Data Load settings control loading behavior rather than the file location.

**Learn more:** [Handling Data source path — Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/handling-resource-path) · [Data sources in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-data-sources)

finalExplanation: The Excel connector’s source location is part of the query’s source definition. Power BI Desktop can update that location through Data source settings, while Power Query can update the path in the Source applied step through the formula bar or directly in the query’s M code through Advanced Editor. Service credential settings control authentication, and Data Load settings control loading behavior rather than the file location.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model containing a table named Table1. Table1 uses Import storage mode.  
  
You need to update the model so that Table1 uses DirectQuery storage mode.  
  
What action should you take?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete Table1, and then add the table to the model again in DirectQuery storage mode.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Power Query Editor, duplicate the query for Table1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From Model view, change the storage mode of Table1 to DirectQuery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add an aggregation table to the model.

definition.explanation:
For most Power BI tables, storage mode is set when the table is added. An Import table cannot be changed directly to DirectQuery; it must be recreated by adding it again with DirectQuery selected. [Microsoft Learn: Table storage mode in Power BI semantic models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-storage-mode)

**Learn more:** [Table storage mode in Power BI semantic models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-storage-mode)

finalExplanation: For most Power BI tables, storage mode is set when the table is added. An Import table cannot be changed directly to DirectQuery; it must be recreated by adding it again with DirectQuery selected. definition.stemRaw:
Case study: Litware, Inc. is an online retailer that uses Power BI. Its data model includes a Sales fact table with sales_date_id and sales_ship_date_id key columns, a Date table, and a Weekly_Returns table. The customer service department requires reports that can be filtered by sales date and ship date independently.

You need to establish relationships that satisfy the customer service department's reporting requirements.

What should you create?

choices.label: A
choices.text: a one-to-many relationship from Date[date_id] to Sales[sales_date_id] and another one-to-many relationship from Date[date_id] to Weekly_Returns[week_id]

choices.label: B
choices.text: a one-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_date_id] to Date[date_id] and a one-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_ship_date_id] to Date[date_id]

choices.label: C
choices.text: an additional date table named ShipDate, a many-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_date_id] to Date[date_id], and a many-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_ship_date_id] to ShipDate[date_id]

choices.label: D
choices.text: an additional date table named ShipDate, a one-to-many relationship from Date[date_id] to Sales[sales_date_id], and a one-to-many relationship from ShipDate[date_id] to Sales[sales_ship_date_id]

finalExplanation: This is a role-playing dimension scenario: the Sales fact table has two independent date roles (sales date and ship date) that the customer service department must be able to filter by simultaneously and independently. Per Microsoft's Power BI modeling guidance, when reports must filter or group by more than one date role at the same time, a single Date table with one active relationship and one inactive relationship (option B) is not sufficient — an inactive relationship can only be activated inside a single measure via USERELATIONSHIP(), which does not support independent, simultaneous slicing/grouping across a visual, and Microsoft's own "Sales" example for that pattern explicitly assumes 'no requirement to simultaneously filter order and ship date periods.' The supported solution for simultaneous, independent filtering is to duplicate the role-playing dimension: add a second date table (here, ShipDate) and give each fact-table date column its own active one-to-many relationship — Date[date_id] → Sales[sales_date_id], and ShipDate[date_id] → Sales[sales_ship_date_id]. Many-to-many relationships (option C) are unnecessary because both key columns are unique per row, and relating Date to the unrelated Weekly_Returns table (option A) does not address the sales-date/ship-date requirement at all.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI report named Orders that supports the following analysis:  
  
- Total sales over time  
- The count of orders over time  
- New and repeat customer counts  
  
The data model size is nearing the limit for a dataset in shared capacity. The model view for the dataset is shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730502414-ee54xl52.jpg)  
  
The data view for the Orders table is shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730505063-dqqxzblr.png)  
  
The Orders table is related to the Customers table by using the CustomerID column. The Orders table is related to the Date table by using the OrderDate column.  
  
For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Summarizing Orders by the CustomerID, OrderID, and OrderDate columns will reduce the model size while still supporting the current analysis.
Removing the CustomerID column from Orders will reduce the model size while still supporting the current analysis.
Removing the UnitPrice and Discount columns from Orders will reduce the model size while still supporting the current analysis.

definition.explanation:
Pre-summarizing an order-line fact table at the CustomerID, OrderID, and OrderDate grain reduces rows while retaining the order, date, customer, and aggregated sales information required for the analysis. CustomerID must remain because it supports the relationship to Customers and distinguishes new from repeat customers. UnitPrice and Discount are unnecessary when SalesTotal is retained for total-sales calculations. Microsoft recommends loading pre-summarized fact data where the resulting grain still supports reporting requirements and removing columns that serve neither reporting nor model-structure purposes.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction)

finalExplanation: Pre-summarizing an order-line fact table at the CustomerID, OrderID, and OrderDate grain reduces rows while retaining the order, date, customer, and aggregated sales information required for the analysis. CustomerID must remain because it supports the relationship to Customers and distinguishes new from repeat customers. UnitPrice and Discount are unnecessary when SalesTotal is retained for total-sales calculations. Microsoft recommends loading pre-summarized fact data where the resulting grain still supports reporting requirements and removing columns that serve neither reporting nor model-structure purposes.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI report with one page. That page includes two line charts and one bar chart.  
  
You need to ensure that users can perform the following actions for all three visuals:  
  
- Switch the measures used in the visuals.  
- Change the visualization type.  
- Add a legend.  
  
The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a bookmark for each acceptable combination of visualization type, measure, and legend in the bar chart.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Edit the interactions between the three visuals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable personalization for the report.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable personalization for each visual.

definition.explanation:
Power BI’s Personalize visuals feature allows report users to swap measures, change the visualization type, and add or remove a legend. Enabling personalization for the report makes all visuals in that report eligible for personalization, minimizing configuration effort.

**Learn more:** [Let users personalize visuals in a report](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/power-bi-personalize-visuals)

finalExplanation: Power BI’s Personalize visuals feature allows report users to swap measures, change the visualization type, and add or remove a legend. Enabling personalization for the report makes all visuals in that report eligible for personalization, minimizing configuration effort.

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating a quick measure as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783732310292-q3uy0nml.png)  
  
You need to create a monthly rolling average measure for Sales over time.  
  
How should you configure the quick-measure calculation?
definition.explanation:
A rolling-average quick measure averages a numeric base measure across a date-based period. Total Sales is the numeric sales measure, Date provides the time axis, and Months sets the rolling window’s unit to months.

**Learn more:** [Use quick measures for common and powerful calculations - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-quick-measures)

finalExplanation: A rolling-average quick measure averages a numeric base measure across a date-based period. Total Sales is the numeric sales measure, Date provides the time axis, and Months sets the rolling window’s unit to months.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model.  
  
You need to configure row-level security (RLS) to limit data access for users with Viewer permissions.  
  
Which three actions should you take, in sequence?

slots.answer: From Microsoft Power BI Desktop, create a new RLS role by using a DAX filter.
From the Power BI service, assign the new RLS role to the users.

items: Assign the users the Contributor role for the Power BI workspace.
Assign the users the Member role for the Power BI workspace.
From the Power BI service, assign the new RLS role to the users.
From Microsoft Power BI Desktop, create a new RLS role by using a DAX filter.
definition.explanation:
Define the RLS role and its DAX table filter in Power BI Desktop, publish the semantic model, and then assign users or security groups to that role in the Power BI service. RLS restricts Viewers, whereas workspace Members and Contributors have edit permissions and RLS does not apply to them.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security) · [Roles in workspaces in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-roles-new-workspaces)

finalExplanation: Define the RLS role and its DAX table filter in Power BI Desktop, publish the semantic model, and then assign users or security groups to that role in the Power BI service. RLS restricts Viewers, whereas workspace Members and Contributors have edit permissions and RLS does not apply to them.

definition.stemRaw:
You are reviewing a Power BI data model.  
  
You have a calculated table with the following definition:  
  
```DAX  
ProductList = INTERSECT ( ProductsGroupA, ProductsGroupB )  
```  
  
You need to determine the result of the DAX expression.  
  
Which rows are returned in `ProductList`?

choices.label: A
choices.text: all the rows in ProductsGroupB that have a matching row in ProductsGroupA

choices.label: B
choices.text: all the rows in both tables

choices.label: C
choices.text: all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have a matching row in ProductsGroupB

choices.label: D
choices.text: all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have no matching row in ProductsGroupB.

definition.explanation:
DAX `INTERSECT` returns the rows from the first table expression that are also present in the second table expression. Therefore, the returned rows originate from `ProductsGroupA` and must have a matching row in `ProductsGroupB`.

**Learn more:** [INTERSECT function (DAX) — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/intersect-function-dax)

finalExplanation: DAX `INTERSECT` returns the rows from the first table expression that are also present in the second table expression. Therefore, the returned rows originate from `ProductsGroupA` and must have a matching row in `ProductsGroupB`.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI dataset containing quarterly sales performance data.  
  
You need to allow managers to review the data in a format that meets these requirements:  
  
- Is optimized for printing.  
- Renders data in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF formats.  
  
What should you create?

choices.label: A
choices.text: a template app

choices.label: B
choices.text: a dashboard

choices.label: C
choices.text: a paginated report

choices.label: D
choices.text: an interactive report

definition.explanation:
Power BI paginated reports are optimized for print-ready, page-oriented layouts and can render in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF formats.

**Learn more:** [When to use paginated reports in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/report-paginated-or-power-bi)

finalExplanation: Power BI paginated reports are optimized for print-ready, page-oriented layouts and can render in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF formats.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI workspace.  
  
You need to create two reports that meet these requirements:  
  
- Report1: Optimized for printing and can be delivered to users through a scheduled email subscription  
- Report2: Optimized for dynamic user interactivity  
  
Which format should you use for each report?
definition.explanation:
Power BI paginated reports (.rdl) are designed for fixed, highly formatted, print-ready output and can be distributed through scheduled email subscriptions. Standard Power BI reports (.pbix) provide interactive visualizations and exploration features such as cross-filtering and drill-through.

**Learn more:** [Paginated Reports in the Power BI Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/explore-reports/end-user-paginated-report) · [Power BI reports overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/power-bi-reports-overview)

finalExplanation: Power BI paginated reports (.rdl) are designed for fixed, highly formatted, print-ready output and can be distributed through scheduled email subscriptions. Standard Power BI reports (.pbix) provide interactive visualizations and exploration features such as cross-filtering and drill-through.

definition.explanation: Teacher First Name is a descriptive attribute of a teacher and belongs in the Teacher dimension. Period Number describes the scheduled class occurrence identified by Class ID, so it belongs in the Class dimension; it supports class counts and attendance analysis by period. Attendance measurements remain in the attendance fact table.

finalExplanation: Teacher First Name is a descriptive attribute of a teacher and belongs in the Teacher dimension. Period Number describes the scheduled class occurrence identified by Class ID, so it belongs in the Class dimension; it supports class counts and attendance analysis by period. definition.stemRaw:
You have four sales regions, each with multiple sales managers.  
  
You implement row-level security (RLS) in a data model and assign the applicable mail-enabled security group to each role.  
  
You have sales reports that allow analysis by region. Sales managers can view sales records for their own region, but are prevented from viewing records for other regions.  
  
A sales manager moves to another region.  
  
You need to ensure that the sales manager can view the correct sales data.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the Microsoft Power BI license type of the sales manager.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Microsoft Power BI Desktop, edit the Row-Level Security setting for the reports.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Manage the permissions of the underlying dataset.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Request that the sales manager be added to the correct Azure Active Directory group.

definition.explanation:
Power BI RLS supports mail-enabled groups as role members. When region access is governed by those groups, changing the manager’s Microsoft Entra ID group membership moves the manager into the role whose row filter permits the new region’s records.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security) · [Row-level security (RLS) guidance in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/rls-guidance)

finalExplanation: Power BI RLS supports mail-enabled groups as role members. When region access is governed by those groups, changing the manager’s Microsoft Entra ID group membership moves the manager into the role whose row filter permits the new region’s records.

To standardize values in the Phone column to 10 digits and exclude country calling codes,

split the column at the right-most occurrence of “)”

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model containing a table named Table1. Table1 has the following columns:  
  
- WebsiteName  
- URL  
  
You need to create a report named Report1 that includes a table visual. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Display the website name.  
- Allow users to navigate to the website's URL by selecting the website name.  
  
What should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: data categories

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conditional Formatting

choices.label: C
choices.text: inline hierarchy labels

choices.label: D
choices.text: URL icons

definition.explanation:
Web URL conditional formatting can format the WebsiteName column as an active hyperlink and use the URL column as the field that supplies each link destination. This displays the website name rather than the raw URL while allowing selection of the name to navigate to that URL.

**Learn more:** [Add hyperlinks (URLs) to a table or matrix - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-za/power-bi/create-reports/power-bi-hyperlinks-in-tables)

finalExplanation: Web URL conditional formatting can format the WebsiteName column as an active hyperlink and use the URL column as the field that supplies each link destination. This displays the website name rather than the raw URL while allowing selection of the name to navigate to that URL.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI report for the procurement department. The report includes data from the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730282838-xd3nrs6m.jpg)

definition.stemRaw: You are creating a financial report in Power BI. The `financials` table includes `Date` and `Sales` columns. Create a measure that calculates the relative sales change compared with the preceding quarter.
definition.template:
Sales QoQ% =

IF(
    ISFILTERED('financials'[Date]),
    ERROR("Uh oh."),
    VAR PREV_QUARTER =
        {{blank1}}(
            SUM('financials'[Sales]),
            {{blank2}}('financials'[Date].[Date], -1, QUARTER)
        )
    RETURN
        {{blank3}}(SUM('financials'[Sales]) - PREV_QUARTER, PREV_QUARTER)
)
definition.explanation:
`CALCULATE` evaluates the sales expression in a modified filter context. `DATEADD` shifts the current date context back one quarter, producing the prior-quarter sales value. `DIVIDE` then returns the relative change as (current sales − prior-quarter sales) divided by prior-quarter sales, while handling a zero denominator safely.

**Learn more:** [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax) · [DATEADD function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/dateadd-function-dax)

finalExplanation: `CALCULATE` evaluates the sales expression in a modified filter context. `DATEADD` shifts the current date context back one quarter, producing the prior-quarter sales value. `DIVIDE` then returns the relative change as (current sales − prior-quarter sales) divided by prior-quarter sales, while handling a zero denominator safely.

You have a Power BI report with the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783729811107-i07pp5zf.png)  
  
You have the following DAX measure.  
  
```DAX  
Accounts :=  
CALCULATE (  
DISTINCTCOUNT (Balances[AccountID]),  
LASTDATE ('Date'[Date])  
```  
  
For each of the following statements, select **Yes** if the statement is true. Otherwise, select **No**.

statements.text: A table visual that displays the date hierarchy at the year level and the [Accounts] measure will show the total number of accounts that were live throughout the year.
A table visual that displays the date hierarchy at the month level and the [Accounts] measure will show the total number of accounts that were live throughout the month.
A table visual that displays the date hierarchy at the day level and the [Accounts] measure will show the total number of accounts that were live that day.

definition.explanation:
LASTDATE returns the final date in the current context, while CALCULATE evaluates its expression in the resulting modified filter context. Therefore, year and month rows represent only the final date of the respective period, not all days in it. A day row has one date in context, so the distinct count represents accounts live on that day.

**Learn more:** [LASTDATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/lastdate-function-dax) · [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax)

finalExplanation: LASTDATE returns the final date in the current context, while CALCULATE evaluates its expression in the resulting modified filter context. Therefore, year and month rows represent only the final date of the respective period, not all days in it. A day row has one date in context, so the distinct count represents accounts live on that day.

Each employee has one manager, as indicated by the ParentEmployeeID column.  
  
All reporting paths lead to the CEO at the top of the organizational hierarchy.  
  
You need to create a calculated column that returns the number of levels from each employee to the CEO.  
  
Which DAX expression should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PATHLENGTH(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]))

choices.label: B
choices.text: PATHITEM(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]),1,INTEGER)

choices.label: C
choices.text: PATHCONTAINS(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]),1)

finalExplanation: `PATH` returns the parent-child path for an employee, and `PATHLENGTH` returns the number of items in that path, including the employee. `PATHLENGTH(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]))` therefore returns the employee's hierarchy level count to the CEO.

• Date  

• Product  

• SalesAmount  
  
You need to create a DAX measure for a rolling 31-day sales total that will return the total sales amount for a selected date and the previous 30 days.  
  
Which DAX expression should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DATEADD(Date[Date], -30, DAY))

choices.label: B
choices.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DATESBETWEEN(Date[Date], Max('Date'[Date])-30, Max('Date'[Date])))

choices.label: C
choices.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DATESMTD(Date[Date]))

choices.label: D
choices.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DISTINCTCOUNT(Date[Date]) = 31)

definition.explanation: DATESBETWEEN creates a continuous date range from 30 days before the maximum date through the maximum date, correctly calculating a rolling 31-day sum. DATEADD alone would incorrectly shift the filter context within the current selection rather than creating an inclusive date range.

finalExplanation: DATESBETWEEN creates a continuous date range from 30 days before the maximum date through the maximum date, correctly calculating a rolling 31-day sum. DATEADD alone would incorrectly shift the filter context within the current selection rather than creating an inclusive date range.

definition.template:
Percent of Product Sales =
VAR ProductSales = SUM ('Sales'[Sales])
VAR AllSales =
{{function1}}(SUM('Sales'[Sales]), {{function2}}('Products'[Product]))
RETURN
DIVIDE (ProductSales, AllSales)
definition.explanation:

You are modifying a Power BI model by using Power BI Desktop. You have a table named Sales that contains the following fields.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730098130-h6u9bppw.jpg)

definition.template:
Transaction Size =

VAR SalesTotal = 'Sales'[Sales]

VAR FilterSegment =
    {{blank1}}(
        {{blank2}}(
            'Transaction Size',
            {{blank3}}(
                'Transaction Size'[Min] <= SalesTotal,
                'Transaction Size'[Max] >= SalesTotal
            )
        )
    )

VAR Result =
    {{blank4}}( DISTINCT ( 'Transaction Size'[Transaction Size] ), FilterSegment )

RETURN
    Result
definition.explanation: FILTER returns the transaction-size row matching the current transaction’s Sales Amount. ALL makes the full Transaction Size table available for the range lookup, AND enforces both inclusive range boundaries, and CALCULATE evaluates the distinct size label under that matching filter.

ALL makes the full Transaction Size table available for the range lookup, AND enforces both inclusive range boundaries, and CALCULATE evaluates the distinct size label under that matching filter.

You need to create a measure that returns the percentage of late orders.  
  
How should you complete the DAX expression?
definition.template:
Late Orders Percent =

VAR OrderCount =
    COUNTROWS ( 'Orders' )

VAR LateOrders =
    {{function}} (
        COUNTROWS ( 'Orders' ),
        {{filter_function}} ( Orders, {{late_condition}} )
    )

RETURN
    DIVIDE ( LateOrders, OrderCount )
definition.explanation:
`COUNTROWS` counts the order rows. `CALCULATE` modifies the filter context for that count, and `FILTER` supplies the row-level predicate. An order is late only when its shipped date is later than its required date, so the predicate is `Orders[ShippedDate] > Orders[RequiredDate]`.

**Learn more:** [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax) · [COUNTROWS function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dax/countrows-function-dax)

finalExplanation: `COUNTROWS` counts the order rows. `CALCULATE` modifies the filter context for that count, and `FILTER` supplies the row-level predicate. An order is late only when its shipped date is later than its required date, so the predicate is `Orders[ShippedDate] > Orders[RequiredDate]`.

choices.text: In the Date query, group by MonthNumber.

definition.stemRaw:
In Power BI Desktop, you are creating a sales report that includes two tables. Row-level security (RLS) is configured on both tables.  
  
You need to create a relationship between the tables. The solution must ensure bidirectional cross-filtering respects the RLS settings.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an inactive relationship between the tables and select Apply security filter in both directions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an active relationship between the tables and select Apply security filter in both directions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an inactive relationship between the tables and select Assume referential integrity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an active relationship between the tables and select Assume referential integrity.

definition.explanation:
RLS filters propagate only through active relationships. Enabling **Apply security filter in both directions** on an active relationship allows the security filter to propagate bidirectionally; **Assume referential integrity** concerns DirectQuery join behavior and does not enable RLS propagation.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security) · [Active vs. inactive relationship guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/relationships-active-inactive)

finalExplanation: RLS filters propagate only through active relationships. Enabling **Apply security filter in both directions** on an active relationship allows the security filter to propagate bidirectionally; **Assume referential integrity** concerns DirectQuery join behavior and does not enable RLS propagation.

Case study context: All of the data sources are cloud-based — an Azure SQL database and Dynamics 365 Business Central (online) — and reports must always reflect current data.

You need to make sure that the data is updated to satisfy the report requirements. The solution must require minimal configuration effort.

What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From each report in powerbi.com, select Refresh visuals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Power BI Desktop, download the PBIX file and refresh the data.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure a scheduled refresh without using an on-premises data gateway.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure a scheduled refresh by using an on-premises data gateway.

definition.explanation: Both data sources — the Azure SQL database and Dynamics 365 Business Central — are cloud-based, so Power BI can refresh the semantic model directly from the cloud without routing through an on-premises data gateway. Configuring scheduled refresh (without a gateway) automatically keeps the reports current with minimal setup. Refreshing visuals (A) does not reload the underlying data, manually re-downloading and refreshing the PBIX (B) is a manual step that must be repeated, and adding an on-premises data gateway (D) is unnecessary extra configuration since no data source is on-premises.

finalExplanation: Both data sources — the Azure SQL database and Dynamics 365 Business Central — are cloud-based, so Power BI can refresh the semantic model directly from the cloud without routing through an on-premises data gateway. Configuring scheduled refresh (without a gateway) automatically keeps the reports current with minimal setup. Refreshing visuals (A) does not reload the underlying data, manually re-downloading and refreshing the PBIX (B) is a manual step that must be repeated, and adding an on-premises data gateway (D) is unnecessary extra configuration since no data source is on-premises.

definition.explanation:
A OneDrive file is stored in SharePoint Online. The SharePoint folder connector can access the workbook as a cloud-based SharePoint source, and the Web connector can access it through its OneDrive online URL. Both avoid relying on a local synchronized file path and can be configured for Power BI service refresh using organizational/OAuth authentication.

**Learn more:** [Use OneDrive for work or school links in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-use-onedrive-business-links) · [Refresh a semantic model created from an Excel workbook on OneDrive or SharePoint Online](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-excel-file-onedrive)

finalExplanation: A OneDrive file is stored in SharePoint Online. The SharePoint folder connector can access the workbook as a cloud-based SharePoint source, and the Web connector can access it through its OneDrive online URL. Both avoid relying on a local synchronized file path and can be configured for Power BI service refresh using organizational/OAuth authentication.

definition.stemRaw:
You publish a dataset that contains data from an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server database.  
  
The dataset needs to refresh daily.  
  
You must ensure that the Power BI service can connect to the database and refresh the dataset.  
  
Which four actions should you perform, in order?

slots.answer: Add the dataset owner to the data source.

items: Add the dataset owner to the data source.
Configure a virtual network data gateway.
definition.explanation:
An on-premises data gateway provides Power BI service connectivity to an on-premises SQL Server source. Create the SQL Server data source on that gateway, then add the dataset owner as a user of the data source; with matching server and database names, the dataset can use the gateway for scheduled refresh. Configure the daily refresh schedule last. A virtual network data gateway is for supported Azure virtual network scenarios, not this on-premises SQL Server setup.

**Learn more:** [Add or remove a gateway data source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/power-bi/connect-data/service-gateway-data-sources) · [Data refresh in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data)

finalExplanation: An on-premises data gateway provides Power BI service connectivity to an on-premises SQL Server source. Create the SQL Server data source on that gateway, then add the dataset owner as a user of the data source; with matching server and database names, the dataset can use the gateway for scheduled refresh. Configure the daily refresh schedule last. A virtual network data gateway is for supported Azure virtual network scenarios, not this on-premises SQL Server setup.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model containing a table named Item. The Item table has a column named Quantity.  
  
Create a DAX query that meets these requirements:  
  
- Calculate item rank based on Quantity values.  
- Do **not** skip ranks when two or more items have the same Quantity value.  
- Display a blank Quantity total when an item is not filtered.  
  
How should you complete the DAX formula?
definition.template:
Item Quantity Rank =
IF(
    {{function}} ('Item'[Item]),
    RANKX(
        ALL('Item'[Item]),
        [Quantity],
        ,
        ,
        {{ties}}
    )
)
definition.explanation:
HASONEVALUE returns true only when the Item filter context contains one distinct item; when it does not, IF returns BLANK(). RANKX evaluates Quantity over ALL('Item'[Item]) so the rank is compared with all items. The DENSE ties option gives tied values the same rank and assigns the next consecutive rank to the following distinct value.

**Learn more:** [HASONEVALUE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/hasonevalue-function-dax) · [RANKX function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/rankx-function-dax)

finalExplanation: HASONEVALUE returns true only when the Item filter context contains one distinct item; when it does not, IF returns BLANK(). RANKX evaluates Quantity over ALL('Item'[Item]) so the rank is compared with all items. The DENSE ties option gives tied values the same rank and assigns the next consecutive rank to the following distinct value.

definition.stemRaw:
You plan to create a Power BI semantic model named Model1 that will contain data from an Azure SQL database.  
  
Model1 will include the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783745252018-drd68vqj.png)  
  
You create DimDate and DimProduct by using Import storage mode.  
  
Configure the storage mode for each remaining table so that:  
  
- FactSales data is available within five minutes after it becomes available in the source data.  
- Report query response time for connections to the model is minimized.  
  
Which storage mode should you configure for each table?
definition.explanation:
DirectQuery keeps the large, once-per-minute FactSales table at the source and supports near-real-time results. Dual is appropriate for the DimCustomer dimension because it can serve cached dimension queries efficiently and participate in efficient source queries with the DirectQuery fact table. Import is fastest for the small FactMarketingEmail table, whose daily changes do not require near-real-time reporting.

**Learn more:** [Composite model guidance in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/composite-model-guidance) · [Table storage mode in Power BI semantic models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-storage-mode)

finalExplanation: DirectQuery keeps the large, once-per-minute FactSales table at the source and supports near-real-time results. Dual is appropriate for the DimCustomer dimension because it can serve cached dimension queries efficiently and participate in efficient source queries with the DirectQuery fact table. Import is fastest for the small FactMarketingEmail table, whose daily changes do not require near-real-time reporting.

You have the Power BI data model shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783732310477-1h19ogum.png)  
  
The Sales table contains daily sales records for the last five years, through today’s date.  
  
You plan to create a measure that returns total sales for March 2021 when March 2022 is selected.  
  
Which DAX expression should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calculate (Sum(Sales[Sales]), PREVIOUSYEAR( dimDate[Date])

choices.label: B
choices.text: TOTALYTD (SUM(Sales[Sales]), dimDate[Date] )

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calculate (SUM(Sales[Sales]), SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(dimDate[Date] ))

choices.label: D
choices.text: SUM(Sales[Sales])

definition.explanation:
`SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(dimDate[Date])` returns the dates in the current filter context shifted back one year. Used as a filter argument to `CALCULATE`, it changes a March 2022 selection to March 2021 while `SUM(Sales[Sales])` aggregates the related sales rows.

**Learn more:** [SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dax/sameperiodlastyear-function-dax)

finalExplanation: `SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(dimDate[Date])` returns the dates in the current filter context shifted back one year. Used as a filter argument to `CALCULATE`, it changes a March 2022 selection to March 2021 while `SUM(Sales[Sales])` aggregates the related sales rows.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft Power BI report. The PBIX file size is 550 MB. The report is accessed through an App workspace in the shared capacity of powerbi.com.  
  
The report uses an imported dataset containing one fact table. The fact table contains 12 million rows. The dataset is scheduled to refresh twice daily, at 08:00 and 17:00.  
  
The report has a single page containing 15 AppSource visuals and 10 default visuals. Users report that visuals load slowly when they access and interact with the report.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to improve report performance. What should you recommend?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change any DAX measures to use iterator functions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable visual interactions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace the default visuals with AppSource visuals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Split the visuals onto multiple pages.

definition.explanation:
Reducing the number of visuals on a report page reduces the visuals that must load initially and the queries or rendering work triggered by interactions. A page with 25 visuals, particularly many custom AppSource visuals, can have substantial client-side and visual-query overhead. Splitting the visuals across multiple pages therefore improves load and interaction performance.

**Learn more:** [Customize the Visualizations Pane in Power BI Desktop and the Power BI Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-report-visualizations) · [Use Performance Analyzer to Examine Report Performance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/performance-analyzer)

finalExplanation: Reducing the number of visuals on a report page reduces the visuals that must load initially and the queries or rendering work triggered by interactions. A page with 25 visuals, particularly many custom AppSource visuals, can have substantial client-side and visual-query overhead. Splitting the visuals across multiple pages therefore improves load and interaction performance.

You use Power BI Desktop to create a report named RPT1 that imports data from a Microsoft Excel file named File1. File1 is stored on a network share.  
  
File1 is moved to another folder.  
  
When you open RPT1 in Power BI Desktop, you find that the report shows outdated data.  
  
You need to ensure that the data in File1 refreshes correctly.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the data source.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clear the permissions of File1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Export a PBIDS file.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Modify the permissions for File1.

definition.explanation:
Power BI Desktop refreshes imported data by connecting to the configured underlying data source. When an Excel file is moved, the saved network-file path no longer points to the workbook, so the report’s data source must be changed to the file’s new location before current data can refresh.

**Learn more:** [Data sources in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-data-sources) · [Data refresh in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data)

finalExplanation: Power BI Desktop refreshes imported data by connecting to the configured underlying data source. When an Excel file is moved, the saved network-file path no longer points to the workbook, so the report’s data source must be changed to the file’s new location before current data can refresh.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model that contains four queries named Query 1, Query2. Query3, and Query4.  
  
Query1 loads customer data into the model and is referenced by the other three queries.  
  
You discover that data refresh for the model is slow.  
  
You need to improve the data refresh time. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run the Table.buffer function in Query1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Duplicate Query1 to all the other queries.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reconfigure Query1 as a dataflow entity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From the Power BI Admin portal, increase the Capacity settings.

definition.explanation:
Microsoft's own guidance on referenced queries states that when several queries reference a shared query like Query1, each referencing query re-executes Query1's steps independently, and explicitly warns that wrapping Query1 in Table.Buffer does not eliminate this duplicate retrieval and can even worsen performance since each referencing query buffers it separately. The recommended fix is to redesign Query1 as a dataflow entity so its data is persisted and evaluated once, which the other queries then reuse — improving refresh time without the added cost of increasing capacity.

**Learn more:** [Referencing Power Query queries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/power-query-referenced-queries)

finalExplanation: Microsoft's own guidance on referenced queries states that when several queries reference a shared query like Query1, each referencing query re-executes Query1's steps independently, and explicitly warns that wrapping Query1 in Table.Buffer does not eliminate this duplicate retrieval and can even worsen performance since each referencing query buffers it separately. The recommended fix is to redesign Query1 as a dataflow entity so its data is persisted and evaluated once, which the other queries then reuse — improving refresh time without the added cost of increasing capacity.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI data model that imports data from a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet.  
  
You use Power Query to load a query containing both renamed and custom columns.  
  
Later, you try to reload the query and receive this error message:  
  
`Expression.Error: The column 'Category' of the table wasn't found.`  
  
What are two possible causes of the error? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The column was removed from the source file.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The column was renamed in the source file.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The file is no longer in the specified location.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The data type of the column was changed.

definition.explanation:
Power Query raises this error when an applied step directly references a column name that no longer exists in the input table. Removing `Category` from the source or renaming it in the source prevents a rename, custom-column, or other dependent step from finding that column. A missing or moved file produces a source-access error instead, while changing a column’s data type does not make its name unavailable.

**Learn more:** [Dealing with errors in Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/dealing-with-errors)

finalExplanation: Power Query raises this error when an applied step directly references a column name that no longer exists in the input table. Removing `Category` from the source or renaming it in the source prevents a rename, custom-column, or other dependent step from finding that column. A missing or moved file produces a source-access error instead, while changing a column’s data type does not make its name unavailable.

definition.stemRaw: You need to create a measure that returns the percentage of revenue by product category. How should you complete the measure?

VAR AllCategoryRev =
{{b1}}(SUM ([Revenue]),

{{b2}}(ProductList[ProductCategory]))

RETURN

You have a Power BI semantic model.  
  
You need to create a column that contains year-over-year (YOY) revenue. The column must contain a ratio of the change factor compared to the previous year's monthly revenue.  
  
How should you complete the DAX formula?
definition.template:
Revenue YoY % =

VAR RevenuePriorYear = CALCULATE([Revenue], {{time_function}}('Date'[Date]))

RETURN
{{calculation_function}}(
    [Revenue] - RevenuePriorYear,

    RevenuePriorYear
)
definition.explanation:
SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the current date context back one year while retaining the corresponding monthly period. DIVIDE calculates the year-over-year change ratio by dividing the revenue difference by prior-year revenue and safely handles a zero denominator.

You use Power BI Desktop to load data from a Microsoft SQL Server database.  
  
While you wait for the data to load, the following error appears.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783732328654-a5dojjw9.png)  
  
You need to fix the error.  
  
Which two actions can achieve this goal? Each correct answer is a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduce the number of rows and columns returned by each query.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Split log running queries into subsets of columns and use Power Query to merge the queries.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Power Query to combine log running queries into one query.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable query folding on long running queries.

definition.explanation:
Reducing returned rows and columns lowers the volume of data that SQL Server and Power BI must process and transfer, helping the query complete before the timeout. Splitting a long-running query into narrower column subsets and merging the results in Power Query can likewise reduce the workload and payload of each individual query. Query folding should generally be preserved for relational sources because it pushes eligible transformations to the data source and improves refresh performance.

**Learn more:** [Best practices when working with Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/best-practices) · [Query folding guidance in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/power-query-folding)

finalExplanation: Reducing returned rows and columns lowers the volume of data that SQL Server and Power BI must process and transfer, helping the query complete before the timeout. Splitting a long-running query into narrower column subsets and merging the results in Power Query can likewise reduce the workload and payload of each individual query. Query folding should generally be preserved for relational sources because it pushes eligible transformations to the data source and improves refresh performance.

- Sales Order ID  
- Freight Amount  
- Subtotal Amount

The Sales Order ID column uniquely identifies every sales order. The Subtotal Amount and Total Item Quantity columns are always populated, whereas the Tax Amount and Freight Amount columns can be null when an order has no associated amount.  
  
You need to query the data to identify these metrics by month:  
  
- The average item quantity per order  
- The average freight amount per order  
- The maximum item quantity per order

Replacing null Freight Amount values with 0 records their actual zero freight while retaining every sales order in the average denominator. The item-quantity values are already populated, and Tax Amount does not affect any requested metric.

**Learn more:** [Append queries (Power Query)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/append-queries) · [Manage queries in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-query-manage)

The report uses an imported dataset that contains one fact table. The fact table has 12 million rows. The dataset is scheduled to refresh twice daily at 08:00 and 17:00.  
  
The report consists of a single page containing 15 AppSource visuals and 10 default visuals.  
  
Users report that the visuals load slowly when they access and interact with the report.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to improve the report's performance.  
  
What should you recommend?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Replace the default visuals with AppSource visuals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove unused columns from tables in the data model.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the imported dataset to DirectQuery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the number of times that the dataset is refreshed.

definition.explanation:
Removing unused columns reduces the size and memory consumption of an imported Power BI model and can improve query performance for visuals. Model columns should be retained only when required for reporting or model structure; unnecessary columns add storage and processing overhead. DirectQuery can introduce source-query latency, and more frequent refreshes improve freshness rather than interactive report rendering.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction)

finalExplanation: Removing unused columns reduces the size and memory consumption of an imported Power BI model and can improve query performance for visuals. Model columns should be retained only when required for reporting or model structure; unnecessary columns add storage and processing overhead. DirectQuery can introduce source-query latency, and more frequent refreshes improve freshness rather than interactive report rendering.

You use Power Query Editor to import three tables named Customers, Address, and Country.  
  
In the source system, not every customer has a related address, but every address has a related country.  
  
You must merge all tables into one query while optimizing query-refresh performance.

definition.explanation:
A right outer join of Customers to Address keeps every Address row and adds the matching Customer data; it does not retain customers that have no address. Because each Address row has a related Country row, an inner join between Address and Country retains every required address-country combination while avoiding unmatched-row processing.

**Learn more:** [Merge Queries Overview - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-overview) · [JoinKind.Type - PowerQuery M](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powerquery-m/joinkind-type)

finalExplanation: A right outer join of Customers to Address keeps every Address row and adds the matching Customer data; it does not retain customers that have no address. Because each Address row has a related Country row, an inner join between Address and Country retains every required address-country combination while avoiding unmatched-row processing.

From powerbi.com, add a tile for the Excel1 dataset to DashboardA.

items: From powerbi.com, pin a range from Excel1 to DashboardA.
From Excel, format the data in Excel1 as a table.
From powerbi.com, import Excel1 as a dataset.
From powerbi.com, add a tile for the Excel1 dataset to DashboardA.
From Excel, create a named range by using the data in Excel1.
definition.explanation:
Power BI Q&A works against a dataset (semantic model), and it only appears on a dashboard when that dashboard has a tile pinned from the dataset, so you must expose Excel1 as a dataset and give the dashboard a tile from it. First you format the range in Excel as a table so the data is Q&A-friendly and importable, then from powerbi.com you import Excel1 as a dataset, and finally you add a tile for that dataset to DashboardA, which lights up Q&A for users of the dashboard. "Upload Excel1" is redundant with "import as a dataset" and does not by itself attach the data to the dashboard for Q&A, which is why the automated key's sequence is wrong.

**Learn more:** [Publish to Power BI from Excel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-publish-from-excel) · [Prepare Excel data for Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-prepare-data-for-q-and-a)

definition.stemRaw:
You need to create a date table in Power BI that contains 10 complete calendar years, including the current year.  
  
How should you complete the DAX expression?
definition.template:
Date =
var var1 = {{fn_year}}({{fn_today}}())
return
{{fn_calendar}}(
    DATE(var1 -9, 01, 01),
    DATE(var1, 12, 31)
)
definition.explanation:
`YEAR(TODAY())` obtains the current year. `CALENDAR` returns the inclusive date range from January 1 nine years before that year through December 31 of the current year, yielding 10 complete calendar years.

**Learn more:** [CALENDAR function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calendar-function-dax) · [TODAY function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/dax/today-function-dax)

finalExplanation: `YEAR(TODAY())` obtains the current year. `CALENDAR` returns the inclusive date range from January 1 nine years before that year through December 31 of the current year, yielding 10 complete calendar years.

definition.stemRaw:
You need to create the semantic model.  
  
Which storage mode should you use for the tables in the semantic model?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DirectQuery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dual

choices.label: C
choices.text: Import

choices.label: D
choices.text: live connection

definition.explanation:
Because the source data only needs to be refreshed once a day at a fixed early-morning time and reports must respond quickly while enforcing row-level security, importing all tables into the in-memory model gives the best query performance and full RLS support. DirectQuery would query the source on every interaction (unnecessary given the fixed refresh schedule) and does not support row-level security the way Import does, so Import is the appropriate storage mode for every table.

**Learn more:** [Storage mode in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-storage-mode)

finalExplanation: Because the source data only needs to be refreshed once a day at a fixed early-morning time and reports must respond quickly while enforcing row-level security, importing all tables into the in-memory model gives the best query performance and full RLS support. DirectQuery would query the source on every interaction (unnecessary given the fixed refresh schedule) and does not support row-level security the way Import does, so Import is the appropriate storage mode for every table.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft Fabric eventhouse named Eventhouse1 that contains high-velocity, high-volume data from IoT devices.  
  
Eventhouse1 can be queried to provide data to reports in near-real-time (NRT).  
  
You plan to use Power BI Desktop to create a report that will include both historical and live data.  
  
You need to connect to Eventhouse1. The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Build a composite model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use DirectQuery connectivity mode.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Import connectivity mode.

definition.explanation:
Power BI DirectQuery queries the Eventhouse KQL database directly and is the recommended connectivity mode for large datasets or when near-real-time data is needed. It provides access to retained historical data and newly ingested live data without the extra model design required for a composite model.

**Learn more:** [Connect KQL Database to Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Fabric](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/real-time-intelligence/power-bi-data-connector)

finalExplanation: Power BI DirectQuery queries the Eventhouse KQL database directly and is the recommended connectivity mode for large datasets or when near-real-time data is needed. It provides access to retained historical data and newly ingested live data without the extra model design required for a composite model.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a Power BI report that uses data from an Azure SQL database named `erp1`.  
  
You import the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730275212-4fcvg83r.jpg)  
  
You need to perform these analyses:  
  
- Orders sold over time that include a measure of total order value  
- Orders by attributes of the products sold  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730277310-9pbw6stx.png)  
  
The solution must minimize visual-interaction update times in the report.  
  
What should you do first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Power Query, merge the Order Line Items query and the Products query.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a calculated column that adds a list of product categories to the Orders table by using a DAX function.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calculate the count of orders per product by using a DAX function.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From Power Query, merge the Orders query and the Order Line Items query.

definition.explanation:
A fact table should store data at a consistent transaction grain and contain values that can be aggregated, while dimension tables provide attributes for filtering and grouping. Merging Orders into Order Line Items adds the order-level time attributes to the line-level quantity and price data, creating a sales fact table suitable for total-order-value measures and time analysis. Keeping Products separate allows product attributes to filter that fact table through an efficient one-to-many relationship, consistent with a star schema.

**Learn more:** [Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/star-schema)

finalExplanation: A fact table should store data at a consistent transaction grain and contain values that can be aggregated, while dimension tables provide attributes for filtering and grouping. Merging Orders into Order Line Items adds the order-level time attributes to the line-level quantity and price data, creating a sales fact table suitable for total-order-value measures and time analysis. Keeping Products separate allows product attributes to filter that fact table through an efficient one-to-many relationship, consistent with a star schema.

**Learn more:** [How to integrate with Power BI to build analytics reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/industry/training-services/microsoft-community-training/ga-version/analytics/custom-reports/power-bi-integration)

finalExplanation: Power BI Desktop Data source settings lets an author select an existing data source and use **Change Source** to specify the replacement server and database. Updating the shared Azure SQL connection centrally avoids modifying the source step of every individual query.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783740441843-byok8bck.png)  
  
You need to change the default colors of all three visuals to make the report more accessible to users who have color vision deficiency.

choices.label: B

definition.explanation:

Updating just these two palettes to color-blind-safe hues fixes the default colors across all three visuals; Theme colors govern categorical series, which none of these visuals rely on for their default coloring.

**Learn more:** [Use report themes in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-report-themes)

finalExplanation: The report's KPI card and waterfall chart both draw their green/red/blue status colors from the theme's Sentiment colors setting (good/bad/neutral and increase/decrease/total), while the table's background color scale on the Actual Amount column comes from the Divergent colors setting used for conditional-formatting gradients. Updating just these two palettes to color-blind-safe hues fixes the default colors across all three visuals; Theme colors govern categorical series, which none of these visuals rely on for their default coloring.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI query named `Expenses` that imports the following data.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783742188888-wn0tjh0x.png)  
  
Users use only the date portion of the `TransactionDate` value when performing data analysis.  
  
You need to minimize the model size without affecting the analysis.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the data type of the TransactionDate column to Date.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the data type of the PostDate column to Date.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove the PostDate column.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove the TransactionID column.

definition.explanation:
Changing `TransactionDate` to the Date type removes the unneeded time component while preserving date-based analysis. Removing the unused `PostDate` column eliminates its storage from the imported model. Optimizing column data types and removing unneeded columns reduce an Import model’s size.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction) · [Data types in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-data-types)

finalExplanation: Changing `TransactionDate` to the Date type removes the unneeded time component while preserving date-based analysis. Removing the unused `PostDate` column eliminates its storage from the imported model. Optimizing column data types and removing unneeded columns reduce an Import model’s size.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model named Model1.  
  
You have a Power BI report named Report1 that includes a single imported table named Sales. Sales has a column named SalesAmount and a column named OrderDate. The Sales table has 1.5 billion rows.  
  
You determine that Model1 is too large and cannot refresh within the defined time.  
  
You need to decrease the size of Model1. The solution must ensure that you can create visuals showing the sum of SalesAmount over time.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Power Query, remove the SalesAmount column from the Sales table.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Power Query, remove the OrderDate column from the Sales table.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In Report1, filter the Sales table to include only rows from the current year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From Power Query, group the Sales table by OrderDate and aggregate SalesAmount.

definition.explanation:
Pre-summarizing fact data is an effective way to reduce an Import model’s size. Grouping Sales by OrderDate and aggregating SalesAmount preserves the date-level totals needed for time-based sum visuals while eliminating the detailed transaction rows, substantially reducing row count and refresh workload.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/mt-mt/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction)

finalExplanation: Pre-summarizing fact data is an effective way to reduce an Import model’s size. Grouping Sales by OrderDate and aggregating SalesAmount preserves the date-level totals needed for time-based sum visuals while eliminating the detailed transaction rows, substantially reducing row count and refresh workload.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a query called All Sales that imports sales data into a Power BI model.  
  
You plan to build a star schema by splitting columns into separate queries and applying additional transformations. The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Use All Sales as the source for three other queries named Sales Fact, Product Dimension, and Customer Dimension.  
- Minimize maintenance effort.  
  
What should you do to create the Sales Fact query, and for which query should you clear **Enable load**?
definition.explanation:
A reference creates a new query that uses the original query’s steps, and changes to the original flow to the referenced query. Referencing All Sales therefore avoids duplicated logic for the fact and dimension queries. Disable load on the intermediate All Sales query so it remains available to downstream queries without adding an unnecessary table to the data model.

**Learn more:** [Referencing Power Query queries - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/power-bi/guidance/power-query-referenced-queries) · [Diagram view - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/diagram-view)

finalExplanation: A reference creates a new query that uses the original query’s steps, and changes to the original flow to the referenced query. Referencing All Sales therefore avoids duplicated logic for the fact and dimension queries. Disable load on the intermediate All Sales query so it remains available to downstream queries without adding an unnecessary table to the data model.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model named Model1.  
  
You need to create a measure that displays the sales result for all blue units. The solution must preserve the existing filter context.  
  
How should you complete the DAX expression?
definition.template:
Sales =
    {{function}}(
        [Sales],
        {{filter_modifier}}('Unit'[Color] = "blue")
    )
definition.explanation:
CALCULATE evaluates the measure with a filter argument. KEEPFILTERS adds the blue color condition by intersecting it with any existing filter on the same column, rather than replacing that filter context.

**Learn more:** [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax) · [KEEPFILTERS function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/keepfilters-function-dax)

finalExplanation: CALCULATE evaluates the measure with a filter argument. KEEPFILTERS adds the blue color condition by intersecting it with any existing filter on the same column, rather than replacing that filter context.

Create a measure that returns year-to-date total sales for the equivalent date in the preceding calendar year.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model that imports data from a Microsoft SQL Server database and an Oracle database. The semantic model is deployed to the Power BI service. Parameters are already in use for the SQL Server data source.  
  
You plan to make a change to the semantic model to ensure consistent behavior across all data sources.  
  
You need to enable parameterization for the Oracle data source. The solution must minimize changes to the existing model.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Power BI Desktop, modify the Oracle data source to use a parameter, and then republish the model to the Power BI service.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From the Power BI service, modify the parameters of the SQL Server data source.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From the Power BI service, create a new semantic model that uses the existing model as a data source, and then parameterize the new model.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From the Power BI service, set a parameter value for the model.

definition.explanation:
Power BI report creators define query parameters in Power BI Desktop. After publishing, the Power BI service can review and change existing parameter settings, but it cannot create a new parameter. Adding a parameter to the Oracle connection in the existing Desktop model and republishing provides consistent parameterization while avoiding creation of another semantic model.

**Learn more:** [Edit parameter settings in the Power BI service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-parameters) · [Publish semantic models and reports from Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-upload-desktop-files)

finalExplanation: Power BI report creators define query parameters in Power BI Desktop. After publishing, the Power BI service can review and change existing parameter settings, but it cannot create a new parameter. Adding a parameter to the Oracle connection in the existing Desktop model and republishing provides consistent parameterization while avoiding creation of another semantic model.
