definition.stemRaw:
You have data in a Microsoft Excel worksheet, as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783735454433-uarwp1bj.png)  
  
You need to use Power Query to clean and transform the dataset. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- If the discount column returns an error, a discount of 0.05 must be used.  
- All data rows must be retained.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
What should you do in Power Query Editor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select Replace Errors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Edit the query in the Query Errors group.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Select Remove Errors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Select Keep Errors.

definition.explanation:
Power Query's **Replace Errors** operation substitutes each cell-level error in the selected discount column with a specified fixed value, such as 0.05, without removing any rows. This satisfies both the replacement requirement and the requirement to retain all data rows.

**Learn more:** [Dealing with errors - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/dealing-with-errors)

finalExplanation: Power Query's **Replace Errors** operation substitutes each cell-level error in the selected discount column with a specified fixed value, such as 0.05, without removing any rows. This satisfies both the replacement requirement and the requirement to retain all data rows.

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating a Power BI model and report.  
  
You have one table in the data model, named Product. Product contains these fields:  
  
- ID  
- Name  
- Color  
- Category  
- Total Sales  
  
You need to create a calculated table that displays only the top eight products by the highest Total Sales value.  
  
How should you complete the DAX expression? Each value may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
definition.template: Top 8 Products = {{function}} (8, 'Product', 'Product'[Total Sales], {{sort_order}})
definition.explanation:
TOPN returns the specified number of rows from a table according to an ordering expression. Ordering Product[Total Sales] with DESC selects the products with the highest sales values.

definition.stemRaw: Which DAX expression should be used to obtain the ending balances in balance sheet reports?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CALCULATE ( SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), LASTDATE ( 'Date'[Date] ) )

choices.label: B
choices.text: CALCULATE ( SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), DATESQTD('Date'[Date]) )

choices.label: C
choices.text: FIRSTNONBLANK ('Date'[Date] SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ) )

choices.label: D
choices.text: CALCULATE ( MAX( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), LASTDATE ('Date'[Date] ))

definition.explanation:
`LASTDATE('Date'[Date])` returns the last date in the current date context and can be applied by `CALCULATE` as a table filter. Summing `BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount]` under that filter yields the balance recorded on the ending date, rather than a quarter-to-date total or the numerically greatest balance. [Microsoft Learn: LASTDATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/lastdate-function-dax)

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Learn: LASTDATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/lastdate-function-dax)

finalExplanation: `LASTDATE('Date'[Date])` returns the last date in the current date context and can be applied by `CALCULATE` as a table filter. Summing `BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount]` under that filter yields the balance recorded on the ending date, rather than a quarter-to-date total or the numerically greatest balance. [Microsoft Learn: LASTDATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/lastdate-function-dax)

definition.stemRaw:
You are building a visual in a Power BI report. The related semantic model includes sales for three products over the past four years.  
  
You need to show total sales by quarter, grouped by product. The visual must show trends for both overall sales and sales for each individual product.  
  
Which visual type should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: area chart

choices.label: B
choices.text: clustered column chart

choices.label: C
choices.text: stacked area chart

choices.label: D
choices.text: line chart

definition.explanation:
A stacked area chart displays time-based trends for multiple product series while stacking their values. The stacked segments reveal each product’s sales trend and contribution, and the combined stack height shows the total sales trend for each quarter. Microsoft documents that stacked area charts can show cumulative totals and that they are suited to showing totals for all series together with each series’ contribution.

**Learn more:** [Overview of visualizations in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-visualizations-overview) · [Area Charts in Power BI Paginated Reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/paginated-reports/report-design/visualizations/area-charts-report-builder)

finalExplanation: A stacked area chart displays time-based trends for multiple product series while stacking their values. The stacked segments reveal each product’s sales trend and contribution, and the combined stack height shows the total sales trend for each quarter. Microsoft documents that stacked area charts can show cumulative totals and that they are suited to showing totals for all series together with each series’ contribution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a security role that has a table filter on the Sales Manager table where username = sales_manager_id.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a security role that has a table filter on the Region Manager table where sales_manager_id = UserPrincipalName().

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a security role that has a table filter on the Sales_Manager table where name = UserName().

definition.explanation:
Dynamic row-level security should filter the Sales Manager mapping table so that only the row whose `username` matches the current user returned by `USERNAME()` is visible. The model relationships can then propagate that filter to the sales data. Power BI supports dynamic RLS rules that use `USERNAME()` or `USERPRINCIPALNAME()`.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security)

finalExplanation: Dynamic row-level security should filter the Sales Manager mapping table so that only the row whose `username` matches the current user returned by `USERNAME()` is visible. The model relationships can then propagate that filter to the sales data. Power BI supports dynamic RLS rules that use `USERNAME()` or `USERPRINCIPALNAME()`.

You have the Power BI model shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730011033-a8saguv8.jpg)  
  
A manager can represent only one country. You need to use row-level security (RLS) to meet these requirements:  
  
- Managers must see data only for their respective country.  
- The number of RLS roles must be minimized.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a single role that filters Country[Manager_Email] by using the USERNAME DAX function.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a single role that filters Country[Manager_Email] by using the USEROBJECTID DAX function.

choices.label: C
choices.text: For the relationship between Purchase Detail and Purchase, select Apply security filter in both directions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create one role for each country.

choices.label: E
choices.text: For the relationship between Purchase and Purchase Detail, change the Cross filter direction to Single.

definition.explanation:
A single dynamic RLS role that filters `Country[Manager_Email]` with `USERNAME()` restricts each manager to the Country row associated with their sign-in identity, minimizing role count. RLS filters use single-directional filtering by default; selecting **Apply security filter in both directions** on the Purchase Detail–Purchase relationship enables the security filter to propagate as required. In the Power BI service, `USERNAME()` returns the user's UPN, which is email-like and can match the manager email column.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security)

finalExplanation: A single dynamic RLS role that filters `Country[Manager_Email]` with `USERNAME()` restricts each manager to the Country row associated with their sign-in identity, minimizing role count. RLS filters use single-directional filtering by default; selecting **Apply security filter in both directions** on the Purchase Detail–Purchase relationship enables the security filter to propagate as required. In the Power BI service, `USERNAME()` returns the user's UPN, which is email-like and can match the manager email column.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable fuzzy matching.

choices.label: C

definition.explanation:

**Learn more:** [Fuzzy merge - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-fuzzy-match) · [Merge queries overview - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-overview)

You use Power Query Editor to retrieve data from a Microsoft SharePoint Online list.  
  
You plan to use Advanced Editor to create a Power Query M formula language query.  
  
You need to create a query that loads the data, expands a column named `Location`, and hides a column named `CountryOrRegion` from the dataset.
definition.template:
let

    Source = SharePoint.Tables("https://contoso.sharepoint.com", [Implementation="2.0", ViewMode="All"]),

    #"3b73bb0e-9677-425e-8296-0f2a756be816" = Source{[Id="3b73bb0e-9677-425e-8296-0f2a756be816"]}[Items],

    #"Expanded Location" = {{expand_location}}(#"3b73bb0e-9677-425e-8296-0f2a756be816", "Location",

in

You have a Power BI semantic model called Model1 that uses Import storage mode.  
  
You need to decrease the size of Model1.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Summarize the detail data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Upgrade to Power BI premium.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implement row-level security (RLS).

choices.label: D
choices.text: Optimize the column data types.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Change the active relationships between tables to inactive relationships.

definition.explanation:
Pre-summarizing detail data reduces the number of fact-table rows retained in the Import model, which can substantially reduce its size. Optimizing column data types can improve VertiPaq storage efficiency; numeric data can use more efficient value encoding than text data in appropriate cases.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling](https://learn.microsoft.com/mt-mt/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction)

finalExplanation: Pre-summarizing detail data reduces the number of fact-table rows retained in the Import model, which can substantially reduce its size. Optimizing column data types can improve VertiPaq storage efficiency; numeric data can use more efficient value encoding than text data in appropriate cases.

Model1 includes the following measure.  
  
```DAX  
Previous Year Sales = CALCULATE([Sales Amount], PREVIOUSYEAR('Date'[Date]))  
```  
  
You have a report that uses Model1. The report contains a single page with a page-level filter set to May 9, 2024. The result of the Previous Year Sales measure is shown in a card visual.  
  
Which value will be displayed in the card visual?
definition.explanation:
`PREVIOUSYEAR` supplies all dates from the prior calendar year for the current date context. For a May 9, 2024 filter, the calculation evaluates 2023 sales: 15 + 20 + 25 = 60.

**Learn more:** [PREVIOUSYEAR function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/previousyear-function-dax)

finalExplanation: `PREVIOUSYEAR` supplies all dates from the prior calendar year for the current date context. For a May 9, 2024 filter, the calculation evaluates 2023 sales: 15 + 20 + 25 = 60.

Workspace Member, Contributor, and Admin roles provide edit capabilities and bypass RLS.

You create a data model in Power BI. Report developers and users say that the data model is too complex. The model contains the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730145100-sjla017q.png)  
  
The model has these relationships:  
  
- There is a one-to-one relationship between Sales_Region and Region_Manager.  
- Manager has more records than Region_Manager, but every Region_Manager record has a corresponding Manager record.  
- Sales_Manager has more records than Sales_Region, but every Sales_Region record has a corresponding Sales_Manager record.  
  
You need to denormalize the model into a single table. Only managers associated with a sales region must be included in reports.  
  
Which three actions should you perform in sequence? Arrange the appropriate actions in the correct order.  
  
More than one order of answer choices is correct; any correct order receives credit.

slots.label: Step 1
slots.answer: Merge [Region_Manager] and [Manager] by using an inner join.

slots.label: Step 2
slots.answer: Merge [Sales_Region] and [Sales_Manager] by using an inner join.

slots.label: Step 3
slots.answer: Merge [Sales_Region] and [Region_Manager] by using an inner join.

items: Merge [Region_Manager] and [Manager] by using an inner join.
Merge [Sales_Manager] and [Sales_Region] by using a left join.
Merge [Sales_Region] and [Sales_Manager] by using an inner join.
Merge [Sales_Region] and [Sales_Manager] by using an inner join as a new query named [Sales_Region_and_Manager].
Merge [Sales_Region] and [Region_Manager] by using a right join as a new query named [Sales_Region_and_Region_Manager].
Merge [Sales_Region] and [Region_Manager] by using an inner join.
definition.explanation:
An inner join retains only matching rows in both tables. Joining Region_Manager to Manager excludes Manager-only records, joining Sales_Region to Sales_Manager excludes Sales_Manager-only records, and joining Sales_Region to Region_Manager retains only associated region-manager records. Expanding the merged columns produces one flattened reporting table containing only managers associated with a sales region.

**Learn more:** [Merge queries overview - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-overview) · [Inner join - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-inner)

finalExplanation: An inner join retains only matching rows in both tables. Joining Region_Manager to Manager excludes Manager-only records, joining Sales_Region to Sales_Manager excludes Sales_Manager-only records, and joining Sales_Region to Region_Manager retains only associated region-manager records. Expanding the merged columns produces one flattened reporting table containing only managers associated with a sales region.

Privacy-level incompatibilities are handled by the Data Privacy Firewall and are distinct from a file-not-found condition.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company employs people in 10 states.  
  
The company recently chose to associate every state with one of the following three regions: East, West, and North.  
  
You have a data model containing employee information by state. The model does **NOT** contain region information.  
  
You have a report that displays employees by state.  
  
You need to view employees by region as quickly as possible.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a new aggregation that summarizes by state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a new aggregation that summarizes by employee.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a new group on the state column and set the Group type to List.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a new group on the state column and set the Group type to Bin.

definition.explanation:
A List group lets selected categorical state values be combined into named groups such as East, West, and North, enabling the report to display employees by the new region grouping without adding region data to the model. Binning is intended for numerical or time fields and does not provide a manual state-to-region mapping.

**Learn more:** [Use grouping and binning in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-grouping-and-binning)

finalExplanation: A List group lets selected categorical state values be combined into named groups such as East, West, and North, enabling the report to display employees by the new region grouping without adding region data to the model. Binning is intended for numerical or time fields and does not provide a manual state-to-region mapping.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model containing the two tables **Dim Location** and **Fact Deliveries**. Their relationships are configured as shown.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783742671040-8i7ec5om.png)  
  
The model includes the following measure:  
  
`Deliveries = COUNTROWS(‘Fact Deliveries’)`  
  
Create a new measure that counts deliveries by destination location.  
  
Each function can be used once, more than once, or not at all.
definition.template:
Deliveries by Destination = {{function}}([Deliveries], {{relationship}}(
    'Dim Location'[Location ID], 'Fact Deliveries'[Destination Location ID]))
definition.explanation:
CALCULATE evaluates [Deliveries] with a modified filter context. USERELATIONSHIP activates the inactive relationship between Dim Location[Location ID] and Fact Deliveries[Destination Location ID] for that calculation, so location filters apply to destination locations rather than the active original-location relationship.

**Learn more:** [USERELATIONSHIP function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/userelationship-function-dax) · [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax)

finalExplanation: CALCULATE evaluates [Deliveries] with a modified filter context. USERELATIONSHIP activates the inactive relationship between Dim Location[Location ID] and Fact Deliveries[Destination Location ID] for that calculation, so location filters apply to destination locations rather than the active original-location relationship.

What should you do in Power BI Desktop?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Power Query, add a date table. Create an active relationship to the OrderDate column in the Orders table and an inactive relationship to the ShippedDate column in the Orders table.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Power Query, add columns to the Orders table to calculate the calendar quarter and the calendar month of the OrderDate column.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From Power BI Desktop, use the Auto date/time option when creating the reports.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From Power Query, use a DAX expression to add columns to the Orders table to calculate the calendar quarter of the OrderDate column, the calendar month of the OrderDate column, the calendar quarter of the ShippedDate column, and the calendar month of the ShippedDate column.

definition.explanation:
A dedicated date table can relate to an Orders fact table by date roles. The OrderDate relationship can be active for default date filtering, while the ShippedDate relationship can remain inactive and be activated in relevant measures by using `USERELATIONSHIP`. This supports calendar-based reporting across both order and shipment dates without adding repeated calendar attributes to the fact table.

**Learn more:** [Active vs inactive relationship guidance - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/relationships-active-inactive) · [Auto date/time guidance in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/auto-date-time)

finalExplanation: A dedicated date table can relate to an Orders fact table by date roles. The OrderDate relationship can be active for default date filtering, while the ShippedDate relationship can remain inactive and be activated in relevant measures by using `USERELATIONSHIP`. This supports calendar-based reporting across both order and shipment dates without adding repeated calendar attributes to the fact table.

The table contains conditional formatting that shows which stores are above, near, or below the monthly quota for returns.  
  
You need to ensure that the table is accessible to consumers of reports who have color vision deficiency.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Move the conditional formatting icons to a tooltip report.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add alt text that lists the values in the table.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the icons to use a different shape for each color.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove the icons and use red, yellow, and green background colors instead.

definition.explanation: For users with color vision deficiency, relying on color alone to convey information is ineffective. Accessibility best practices require non-color visual cues such as distinct shapes or icons to represent different statuses. Changing the icons to use different shapes enables colorblind users to differentiate between stores above, near, or below quota. Moving to tooltips (A) or adding alt text (B) don't make the visual itself accessible, and orange instead of red (D) still relies on color discrimination.

finalExplanation: For users with color vision deficiency, relying on color alone to convey information is ineffective. Accessibility best practices require non-color visual cues such as distinct shapes or icons to represent different statuses. Changing the icons to use different shapes enables colorblind users to differentiate between stores above, near, or below quota. Moving to tooltips (A) or adding alt text (B) don't make the visual itself accessible, and orange instead of red (D) still relies on color discrimination.

You have an imported dataset with a dynamic row-level security (RLS) role named Sales. The Sales role filters sales transaction data by salesperson.  
  
Salespeople must be able to see only data for their own region.  
  
You publish the dataset to powerbi.com, configure RLS role membership, and distribute the dataset and its related reports to the salespeople.  
  
A salesperson says that she believes she should be able to see more data.  
  
You need to verify which data the salesperson currently sees.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the Test as role option to view data as the salesperson's user account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the Test as role option to view data as the Sales role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Instruct the salesperson to open the report in Microsoft Power BI Desktop.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Filter the data in the reports to match the intended logic in the filter on the sales transaction table.

definition.explanation:
Dynamic RLS evaluates access for an individual identity, so verification must use the salesperson’s user account rather than only the generic Sales role. The Power BI service Test as role experience can test a specific person to inspect the data filtered by that person’s effective RLS context.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security)

finalExplanation: Dynamic RLS evaluates access for an individual identity, so verification must use the salesperson’s user account rather than only the generic Sales role. The Power BI service Test as role experience can test a specific person to inspect the data filtered by that person’s effective RLS context.

The file must be imported to a Power BI semantic model.  
  
You need to ensure that the semantic model can be refreshed in PowerBi.com.  
  
Which two connectors can you use to connect to the file? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excel Workbook

choices.label: C
choices.text: Folder

choices.label: D
choices.text: Text/CSV

definition.explanation:
The Excel Workbook connector reads the file directly from its OneDrive location and, because the file lives in the cloud, Power BI can refresh it in the service on a schedule without an on-premises gateway. The SharePoint Folder connector also reaches OneDrive/SharePoint-hosted files and likewise supports scheduled cloud refresh. The Web connector is meant for web page content rather than a specific cloud file, and Folder/Text-CSV don't match a single cloud-hosted Excel workbook.

**Learn more:** [Refresh a semantic model created from an Excel workbook on OneDrive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-excel-file-onedrive)

finalExplanation: The Excel Workbook connector reads the file directly from its OneDrive location and, because the file lives in the cloud, Power BI can refresh it in the service on a schedule without an on-premises gateway. The SharePoint Folder connector also reaches OneDrive/SharePoint-hosted files and likewise supports scheduled cloud refresh. The Web connector is meant for web page content rather than a specific cloud file, and Folder/Text-CSV don't match a single cloud-hosted Excel workbook.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a report containing three pages. One page includes a KPI visualization.  
  
You need to filter every visualization in the report except the KPI visualization.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Edit the interactions of the KPI visualization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the same slicer to each page and configure Sync slicers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Edit the interactions of the slicer that is on the same page as the KPI visualization.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure a page-level filter.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Configure a report-level filter.

definition.explanation:
Synchronized slicers apply a slicer selection to visualizations across the selected report pages. A slicer normally filters the other visuals on its page, but its interaction with a particular visual can be set to **None**. Therefore, synchronize the equivalent slicers across the pages and set the slicer on the KPI page not to filter the KPI. A report-level filter would instead apply to all visuals, including the KPI.

**Learn more:** [Slicers in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-visualization-slicers) · [Add a filter to a report in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/power-bi-report-add-filter)

finalExplanation: Synchronized slicers apply a slicer selection to visualizations across the selected report pages. A slicer normally filters the other visuals on its page, but its interaction with a particular visual can be set to **None**. Therefore, synchronize the equivalent slicers across the pages and set the slicer on the KPI page not to filter the KPI. A report-level filter would instead apply to all visuals, including the KPI.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a CSV file containing user complaints. It has a column named Logged, which records the date and time when each complaint occurred. The Logged data uses this format: `2018-12-31 at 08:59`.  
  
You need to analyze complaints by their logged date and use a built-in date hierarchy.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply the Parse function from the Data transformations options to the Logged column.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the data type of the Logged column to Date.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Split the Logged column by using at as the delimiter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a column by example that starts with 2018-12-31.

definition.explanation:
Splitting the text value at `at` separates the ISO-formatted date from the time. The resulting date field can be recognized as a Date type, which meets Power BI’s requirement for automatically generated date hierarchies. Power BI auto date/time applies to columns whose data type is Date or Date/Time.

**Learn more:** [Auto date/time in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-auto-date-time) · [Data types in Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/data-types)

finalExplanation: Splitting the text value at `at` separates the ISO-formatted date from the time. The resulting date field can be recognized as a Date type, which meets Power BI’s requirement for automatically generated date hierarchies. Power BI auto date/time applies to columns whose data type is Date or Date/Time.

definition.stemRaw:

A user wants daily notifications of the value shown in the card visual.

choices.label: A

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a data alert.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Share the dashboard to the user.

choices.label: D

definition.explanation:
A Power BI dashboard subscription can be scheduled daily and sends the recipient an email containing a snapshot of the dashboard, which includes the card’s displayed value. Data alerts notify only when a value crosses a configured threshold rather than on a fixed daily schedule.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: The SalesRowID and AuditID columns can be removed from the model without impeding the analysis goals.
Both the OrderDateKey and OrderDate columns are necessary to perform the basket analysis.
The TaxAmt column must retain the current number of decimal places to perform the basket analysis.

definition.explanation: SalesRowID and AuditID are technical lineage/load identifiers rather than fields needed to group items into orders or analyze territory. Basket analysis needs the order and product identifiers; dates are not required for the stated analysis, and no date field is required merely to find products bought together. TaxAmt does not affect product co-occurrence, so its current decimal precision need not be retained.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI Desktop semantic model containing a table named Sales. Sales includes these columns:  
  
- OrderDate  
- OrderID  
- ProductID  
- SalesAmount  
  
You create a visual that displays the SalesAmount field over time.  
  
You identify an outlier in the SalesAmount column.  
  
You need to make sure the outlier has as little influence on the visual as possible. The solution must still allow the visual to show overall data trends.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a new column that divides SalesAmount by the highest SalesAmount value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: For the SalesAmount field, set the aggregate type to Median.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable anomaly detection for the visual.

choices.label: D
choices.text: For the SalesAmount field, set the aggregate type to Average.

definition.explanation:
The median is the middle value in an ordered set and is much less affected by an extreme SalesAmount than an arithmetic average or sum. Using Median as the SalesAmount aggregation therefore preserves representative time-based trends while reducing the outlier’s influence.

**Learn more:** [Work with aggregates (sum, average, and so on) in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-aggregates)

finalExplanation: The median is the middle value in an ordered set and is much less affected by an extreme SalesAmount than an arithmetic average or sum. Using Median as the SalesAmount aggregation therefore preserves representative time-based trends while reducing the outlier’s influence.

For the past three days, refresh in Power BI has failed with this error message: “You have reached the maximum allowable memory allocation for your tier. Consider upgrading to a tier with more available memory.”  
  
You need to resolve the error while ensuring query response times are minimized for end users.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Merge the Sales person and invoice tables based on the SalesPersonId column.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the invoice table to a DirectQuery table and read the data live from the source, retaining only the dimension tables as import tables.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the size of the invoice table by summarizing sales by Product, Sales person, Calendar, and Customer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the invoice table to a composite table that contains historical data as a DirectQuery table and hot data as an import table, and then partition the table.

definition.explanation: Summarizing the 12-million-row Invoice fact table by Product, Sales person, Calendar, and Customer reduces the imported model's memory footprint, allowing refresh to fit within the tier allocation. Because the resulting data remains in the in-memory import model, it also provides faster report queries than relying on DirectQuery for fact data.

finalExplanation: Summarizing the 12-million-row Invoice fact table by Product, Sales person, Calendar, and Customer reduces the imported model's memory footprint, allowing refresh to fit within the tier allocation. Because the resulting data remains in the in-memory import model, it also provides faster report queries than relying on DirectQuery for fact data.

What should you do?

choices.label: B

choices.text: Distribute an app to the users in the Azure Active Directory group of the sales department.

A Power BI app is the appropriate mechanism for distributing curated report content to a broad consumer audience, and its audience can be an Azure Active Directory group. Workspace Admin and Member roles grant elevated content-management permissions that are inappropriate for report consumers. Microsoft recommends using app audiences to control the content visible to users or groups.

Workspace Admin and Member roles grant elevated content-management permissions that are inappropriate for report consumers. Microsoft recommends using app audiences to control the content visible to users or groups.

Does this meet the goal?

Solution: You implicitly convert the values into the required type.  
  
Does this meet the goal?

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

definition.explanation: Implicit type conversion does not address case sensitivity or data integrity problems. These issues require explicit data transformation using functions like UPPER() or LOWER(), or correction at the data source level before import.

finalExplanation: Implicit type conversion does not address case sensitivity or data integrity problems. These issues require explicit data transformation using functions like UPPER() or LOWER(), or correction at the data source level before import.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You add an index key and normalize casing in the data source.  
  
Does this meet the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No

definition.explanation:
Power BI's engine is case-insensitive, so when a DirectQuery source is case-sensitive, values differing only by letter case are treated by the source as distinct rows but by Power BI as duplicates, producing undefined values and errors. Normalizing the casing at the data source removes this mismatch, and adding an index key gives each row a stable unique identifier, together resolving the reported issue.

**Learn more:** [Use composite models in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-composite-models)

finalExplanation: Power BI's engine is case-insensitive, so when a DirectQuery source is case-sensitive, values differing only by letter case are treated by the source as distinct rows but by Power BI as duplicates, producing undefined values and errors. Normalizing the casing at the data source removes this mismatch, and adding an index key gives each row a stable unique identifier, together resolving the reported issue.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You normalize casing in the source query or Power Query Editor.  
  
Does this meet the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No

definition.explanation: Normalizing text casing using functions like UPPER() or LOWER() in Power Query standardizes data and resolves case-sensitivity discrepancies. This approach is documented in Microsoft's guidance and prevents undefined values or comparison errors in the model.

finalExplanation: Normalizing text casing using functions like UPPER() or LOWER() in Power Query standardizes data and resolves case-sensitivity discrepancies. This approach is documented in Microsoft's guidance and prevents undefined values or comparison errors in the model.

You need to use Power BI Desktop to make the files’ metadata available as one dataset. The solution must **not** store the JSON files’ data.  
  
Which data source type should you use, and which transformation should you perform?

options: Combine the files of the Content column.

You need to expose the file metadata as one dataset by using Power BI. The solution must **not** store the data from the CSV files.  
  
Which three actions should you carry out, in order?

From Power Query Editor, remove the Content column.
From Power Query Editor, expand the Attributes column.

items: From Power BI Desktop, select Get Data, and then select Folder.

Column quality displays the proportions of valid, error, and empty values in each column. Column profile provides detailed statistics for a selected column, including its maximum value.

**Learn more:** [Data profiling tools](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/data-profiling-tools)

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI model containing two tables named Population and Date.  
  
The Population table has two columns named PopulationAmount and DateKey.  
  
DateKey holds date values representing the first day of a year and is used to create a many-to-one relationship to the Date table.  
  
The Power BI model includes two measures defined as follows:  
  
```DAX  
Total Population = Sum(‘Population’[PopulationAmount])  
2023 Population = CALCULATE([Total Population], ‘Date'[Year] = 2023)  
```  
  
You create a table visual that shows Date[Year] and [2023 Population].  
  
What will the table visual display?

choices.label: A
choices.text: one row per year that contains blank values for every year except 2023

choices.label: B
choices.text: one row per date that contains the population value for the corresponding year repeated in each row

choices.label: C
choices.text: a single row for the year 2023 that contains the related population value

choices.label: D
choices.text: one row per year that contains the same value repeated for each year

definition.explanation: `CALCULATE` replaces an existing filter on `Date[Year]` with the filter `Date[Year] = 2023`. Thus, each year row evaluates the measure using the 2023 date filter and displays the same total population value for 2023.

finalExplanation: `CALCULATE` replaces an existing filter on `Date[Year]` with the filter `Date[Year] = 2023`. Thus, each year row evaluates the measure using the 2023 date filter and displays the same total population value for 2023.

definition.stemRaw:
You publish a semantic model to the Power BI service. The semantic model contains data from the following data sources:  
  
• Source1: A Microsoft Excel file stored in Microsoft OneDrive for Business  

• Source2: An Azure SQL database on a virtual network

Which data sources require an on-premises data gateway?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Source2 only

What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Model view, set the Subject and Body columns to Hidden.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the Subject and Body columns during the import.

choices.text: Implement row-level security (RLS) so that the report recipients can only see results based on the emails they sent.

definition.explanation:
Email-network analysis requires sender and recipient data, not the Subject or Body content. Removing those unnecessary columns during import excludes the sensitive email text from the semantic model and reduces its size. Hidden fields remain in the model and are not a security mechanism; row-level security limits row visibility but does not remove the email-content columns. Microsoft recommends removing columns that do not serve reporting or model-structure requirements.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction) · [Hide or freeze columns in Analysis Services tabular models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/analysis-services/tabular-models/hide-or-freeze-columns-ssas-tabular?view=sql-analysis-services-2025)

finalExplanation: Email-network analysis requires sender and recipient data, not the Subject or Body content. Removing those unnecessary columns during import excludes the sensitive email text from the semantic model and reduces its size. Hidden fields remain in the model and are not a security mechanism; row-level security limits row visibility but does not remove the email-content columns. Microsoft recommends removing columns that do not serve reporting or model-structure requirements.

In Power Query Editor, you have three queries named ProductCategory, ProductSubCategory, and Product.  
  
Every Product has a ProductSubCategory. However, not every ProductsubCategory has a parent ProductCategory.  
  
You must merge the three queries into one query while ensuring the best performance in Power Query. Each merge type may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

**Learn more:** [Merge queries overview - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-overview) · [JoinKind.Type - PowerQuery M](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powerquery-m/joinkind-type)

finalExplanation: An inner join between Product and ProductSubCategory retains all Product rows because each Product has a matching subcategory. A left outer join from ProductSubCategory to ProductCategory preserves subcategories that do not have a parent category, while including category values for matches.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: In Power Query Editor, import the table and then add a filter step to the query.  
  
Does this meet the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No

definition.explanation:
For a relational SQL Server source, Power Query can fold an early filter step into the source query. The filtering is therefore performed by SQL Server before the data is imported, allowing only a sample of the large table to be loaded.

**Learn more:** [Query folding guidance in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/power-query-folding) · [Best practices when working with Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/best-practices)

finalExplanation: For a relational SQL Server source, Power Query can fold an early filter step into the source query. The filtering is therefore performed by SQL Server before the data is imported, allowing only a sample of the large table to be loaded.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You create a DAX expression that uses the `FILTER` function.  
  
Does this meet the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No

definition.explanation:
DAX `FILTER` returns a subset of an existing model table or expression for use in calculations; it does not limit the rows imported from a SQL Server source. To import only a sample during development, filter or otherwise limit the source rowset in Power Query or the source query before loading the table.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction) · [FILTER function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/filter-function-dax)

finalExplanation: DAX `FILTER` returns a subset of an existing model table or expression for use in calculations; it does not limit the rows imported from a SQL Server source. To import only a sample during development, filter or otherwise limit the source rowset in Power Query or the source query before loading the table.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Add a `WHERE` clause to the SQL statement.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No

definition.explanation:
A SQL `WHERE` clause restricts the rows returned by the source query, so Power BI imports only the qualifying subset of the `Order` table rather than all records. Native SQL queries can be used to specify data import.

**Learn more:** [Import data by using a native query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/analysis-services/tabular-models/ssas-import-query?view=sql-analysis-services-2025)

finalExplanation: A SQL `WHERE` clause restricts the rows returned by the source query, so Power BI imports only the qualifying subset of the `Order` table rather than all records. Native SQL queries can be used to specify data import.

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

finalExplanation: A report-level filter applies to all report pages and changes the data displayed by visuals, but it does not reduce the rows loaded during import. A source or query-level filter is required to import only a sample of the SQL Server table.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783729985790-lmkqgzl7.jpg)  
  
Users use only the date portion of the `Sales_Date` field. Only rows whose `Status` is `Finished` are used for analysis.  
  
You need to reduce the query load times without affecting the analysis.  
  
Which two actions achieve this goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove the rows in which Sales[Status] has a value of Canceled.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove Sales[Sales_Date].

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the data type of Sale[Delivery_Time] to Integer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Split Sales[Sale_Date] into separate date and time columns.

Removing `Canceled_Date` also reduces model size because it is not needed for Finished-only analysis. Power BI guidance recommends loading only necessary rows and columns to reduce import-model size and improve load efficiency.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a PBIX file containing sensitive information.  
  
You must secure the information to meet these requirements:  
  
- Only internal users can open the file when it is shared by email.  
- After the file is published, only internal users can open the semantic model and the report downloaded from the Power BI service.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Microsoft Power BI Desktop, apply a sensitivity label.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Certify the semantic model and the report.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a live connection for the file.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From the Power BI service, apply a sensitivity label.

definition.explanation:
A sensitivity label applied in Power BI Desktop can encrypt the PBIX file so that only users with the label’s assigned internal permissions can open it, including when it is emailed. When the labeled PBIX file is published, its label is applied to the resulting report and semantic model, and that protection persists when supported content is downloaded from the Power BI service.

**Learn more:** [Sensitivity Labels in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/powerbi/service-security-sensitivity-label-overview) · [How to apply sensitivity labels in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/powerbi/service-security-apply-data-sensitivity-labels)

finalExplanation: A sensitivity label applied in Power BI Desktop can encrypt the PBIX file so that only users with the label’s assigned internal permissions can open it, including when it is emailed. When the labeled PBIX file is published, its label is applied to the resulting report and semantic model, and that protection persists when supported content is downloaded from the Power BI service.

Which two actions should you take on the Country column? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change Data category to Country.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove duplicate values.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply a clean transform.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replace the empty fields.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Apply a Capitalize Each Word transform.

definition.explanation: A Clean transform removes nonprinting characters that can create invalid or apparently blank country values. Removing duplicate values leaves a single row for each country; Power Query’s duplicate comparison is case-insensitive, so capitalization variants such as Afghanistan and afghanistan are treated as duplicates.

Removing duplicate values leaves a single row for each country; Power Query’s duplicate comparison is case-insensitive, so capitalization variants such as Afghanistan and afghanistan are treated as duplicates.

Each list has over 25,000 rows. Locations is referenced in Customers to create qualified values in a drop-down list.  
  
You create the following query in Power Query Editor.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783745253594-372xvdjg.png)  
  
You notice long load times and find that Power Query Editor calls the URL for every row in the final dataset.  
  
You need to optimize the query while minimizing development effort.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Read the lists separately, and then merge the lists.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Read the lists separately, and then append the lists.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a custom function to read the referenced SharePoint list.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Expand the referenced column of the query.

definition.explanation: Expanding a SharePoint lookup/navigation column can cause Power Query to retrieve the related record separately for each Customers row. Reading Customers and Locations independently and merging them by the lookup identifier retrieves each list once and performs the relationship operation in the query, avoiding per-row calls to the Locations URL.

finalExplanation: Expanding a SharePoint lookup/navigation column can cause Power Query to retrieve the related record separately for each Customers row. Reading Customers and Locations independently and merging them by the lookup identifier retrieves each list once and performs the relationship operation in the query, avoiding per-row calls to the Locations URL.

You have the Power BI model shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730769804-7kj2g7wx.jpg)  
  
There are four departments in the Departments table.  
  
You must ensure that users can view data only for their respective department. What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a slicer that filters Departments based on DepartmentID.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a row-level security (RLS) role for each department, and then define the membership of the role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a DepartmentID parameter to filter the Departments table.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To the ConfidentialData table, add a calculated measure that uses the CURRENTGROUP DAX function.

definition.explanation:
Row-level security (RLS) restricts data access by applying row filters to users assigned to roles. Filtering each department through a separate RLS role, with the appropriate users assigned to that role, limits the visible Department rows and propagates the filter through the one-to-many DepartmentID relationship to the related ConfidentialData rows.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security)

finalExplanation: Row-level security (RLS) restricts data access by applying row filters to users assigned to roles. Filtering each department through a separate RLS role, with the appropriate users assigned to that role, limits the visible Department rows and propagates the filter through the one-to-many DepartmentID relationship to the related ConfidentialData rows.

You need to create reports from the data to identify fraudulent transactions. The data must be visible within five minutes after an update.  
  
How should you configure the data connection?

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set Data Connectivity mode to DirectQuery.

DirectQuery does not import a cached copy of the source data. Report visuals query the underlying Azure SQL database, allowing reports to use current data and supporting near-real-time visibility. [Use DirectQuery in Power BI Desktop — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-use-directquery)

**Learn more:** [Use DirectQuery in Power BI Desktop — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-use-directquery) · [Data refresh in Power BI — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data)

finalExplanation: DirectQuery does not import a cached copy of the source data. Report visuals query the underlying Azure SQL database, allowing reports to use current data and supporting near-real-time visibility. Import mode only reflects source changes after the semantic model is refreshed. definition.stemRaw:
A business intelligence (BI) developer creates a Power BI dataflow that uses DirectQuery to access tables on an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server. The Enhanced Dataflows Compute Engine is enabled for the dataflow.  
  
You need to use the dataflow in a report. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Minimize online processing operations.  
- Minimize calculation and visual-rendering times.  
- Include current-year data through, and including, the prior day.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a dataflows connection that has DirectQuery mode selected.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a dataflows connection that has DirectQuery mode selected and configure a gateway connection for the dataset.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a dataflows connection that has Import mode selected and schedule a daily refresh.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a dataflows connection that has Import mode selected and create a Microsoft Power Automate solution to refresh the data hourly.

definition.explanation:
Import mode loads the dataflow data into the semantic model’s in-memory storage, so report visuals query the imported model rather than issuing online DirectQuery operations at interaction time. This provides faster visual performance. A daily scheduled refresh updates the imported data to include data through the previous day. Microsoft notes that DirectQuery trades up-to-date data for slower report performance, whereas Import mode returns report queries from imported tables and columns.

**Learn more:** [Develop solutions with dataflows — Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/dataflows/dataflows-develop-solutions) · [Data refresh in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data)

finalExplanation: Import mode loads the dataflow data into the semantic model’s in-memory storage, so report visuals query the imported model rather than issuing online DirectQuery operations at interaction time. This provides faster visual performance. A daily scheduled refresh updates the imported data to include data through the previous day. Microsoft notes that DirectQuery trades up-to-date data for slower report performance, whereas Import mode returns report queries from imported tables and columns.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model containing a table named Employees.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783742757857-rajun772.png)  
  
An employee is active when that employee's TermDate column has no value.  
  
You need to create a DAX measure that counts active employees.  
  
How should you complete the DAX expression?
definition.template: Actives = {{function}} (COUNTROWS(Employees), {{condition}} ('Employees' [TermDate]))
definition.explanation:
CALCULATE evaluates an expression in modified filter context. ISBLANK applied to Employees[TermDate] retains only employees with no termination date, and COUNTROWS then counts those active employee rows.

**Learn more:** [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax) · [ISBLANK function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/isblank-function-dax)

finalExplanation: CALCULATE evaluates an expression in modified filter context. ISBLANK applied to Employees[TermDate] retains only employees with no termination date, and COUNTROWS then counts those active employee rows.

definition.stemRaw:
You receive annual sales data that must be included in Power BI reports.  
  
From Power Query Editor, you connect to the Microsoft Excel source shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783732301781-y400r9er.png)  
  
You need to create a report that meets these requirements:  
  
- Visualizes the Sales value over a period of years and months  
- Adds a slicer for the month  
- Adds a slicer for the year  
  
Which three actions should you perform, in sequence?

slots.answer: Select the Month and MonthNumber columns.
Rename the Attribute column as Year and the Value column as Sales.

items: Select the Month and MonthNumber columns.
Rename the Attribute column as Year and the Value column as Sales.
definition.explanation:
Unpivot other columns keeps Month and MonthNumber as identifier fields and changes the year columns into Attribute/Value pairs. Renaming those generated fields to Year and Sales produces a normalized fact table that supports separate Month and Year slicers and a Sales trend across both dimensions.

**Learn more:** [Unpivot columns - Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/unpivot-column) · [Table.UnpivotOtherColumns - PowerQuery M](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powerquery-m/table-unpivotothercolumns)

finalExplanation: Unpivot other columns keeps Month and MonthNumber as identifier fields and changes the year columns into Attribute/Value pairs. Renaming those generated fields to Year and Sales produces a normalized fact table that supports separate Month and Year slicers and a Sales trend across both dimensions.

You have a Power BI report that contains the visual shown in the following exhibit.

You need to make the visual more accessible to users who have color vision deficiency.  
  
What should you do?

choices.text: Change the font color of values in the Sales column to white.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the red background color to orange.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add additional measures to the table values.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add icons to represent the sales status of each product.

definition.explanation: Icons provide non-color visual indicators that users with color vision deficiency can distinguish. Accessibility guidelines prohibit relying on color alone to convey meaning. Font color changes (A) and background color changes (B) still depend on color discrimination. Additional measures (C) do not address the underlying accessibility issue.

finalExplanation: Icons provide non-color visual indicators that users with color vision deficiency can distinguish. Accessibility guidelines prohibit relying on color alone to convey meaning. Font color changes (A) and background color changes (B) still depend on color discrimination. Additional measures (C) do not address the underlying accessibility issue.

A fact table contains dimension key columns that establish its dimensionality. Since Sales retains both SalespersonID and CityID, sales can be summed and grouped by SalespersonID and city after the Salesperson table is removed. The removed table has no attributes beyond SalespersonID, so it provides no additional field required for that analysis. Does this achieve the goal?

Counting sales by salesperson and city requires the Sales rows plus the `SalespersonID` and `CityID` relationship keys. `ProductID` is not required for that grouping or for either active relationship, so it can be removed to reduce the import model size. Does this satisfy the goal?

A fact table requires its dimension key columns to establish relationships and determine its dimensionality. Removing `Sales[CityID]` eliminates the active relationship to `CityData`, so city filters cannot be applied to Sales values. Therefore, total sales cannot be analyzed by salesperson per city.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI table named Customer with a field named Email Address. Multiple records have the same email address.  
  
Create a calculated column that identifies records with duplicate email addresses. Each value may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
definition.template:
Count Email =
VAR Email = [Email Address]
RETURN
    {{function}}(
        {{expression}}(Customer),
        {{filter}}(Customer,
            Customer[Email Address] = Email
        )
    )
definition.explanation:
CALCULATE re-evaluates COUNTROWS(Customer) under a modified filter context built from two filter arguments: ALL(Customer) removes the table's existing filters, and the condition Customer[Email Address] = Email restricts the count to rows sharing the current row's email address. COUNTROWS(Customer) then returns how many records have that email address, so a result greater than one identifies a duplicate.

**Learn more:** [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax) · [ALL function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/all-function-dax)

finalExplanation: CALCULATE re-evaluates COUNTROWS(Customer) under a modified filter context built from two filter arguments: ALL(Customer) removes the table's existing filters, and the condition Customer[Email Address] = Email restricts the count to rows sharing the current row's email address. COUNTROWS(Customer) then returns how many records have that email address, so a result greater than one identifies a duplicate.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model called Model1 that includes a table named Sales. Sales has a column named SalesAmount. Model1 includes a measure named Total Sales that sums the SalesAmount column.  
  
You need to create a measure that reports year-to-date sales revenue for the previous year.  
  
Which DAX formula should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PYTD Sales = CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATEADD(‘Date’[Date], -1, YEAR))

choices.label: B
choices.text: PYTD Sales = CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATEADD(DATESYTD(‘Date’[Date]), -1, YEAR))

choices.label: C
choices.text: PYTD Sales = TOTALYTD([Total Sales], ‘Date’[Date], FILTER(‘Date’, ‘Date’[Date] < TODAY()))

choices.label: D
choices.text: PYTD Sales = CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESYTD(‘Date’[Date]))

definition.explanation:
`DATESYTD` returns the year-to-date dates in the current context. `DATEADD(..., -1, YEAR)` shifts that entire date range back one year, and `CALCULATE` evaluates `Total Sales` over the shifted range, producing previous-year year-to-date revenue.

**Learn more:** [DATESYTD function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/datesytd-function-dax) · [Time intelligence functions (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/time-intelligence-functions-dax)

finalExplanation: `DATESYTD` returns the year-to-date dates in the current context. `DATEADD(..., -1, YEAR)` shifts that entire date range back one year, and `CALCULATE` evaluates `Total Sales` over the shifted range, producing previous-year year-to-date revenue.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Power BI semantic model that connects to a streaming data source. The data source is updated frequently.  
  
You need to create a Power BI report that meets the following requirements:  
  
• Supports real-time analytics  

• Minimizes performance impact on the data source  

• Displays the most recent data without performing a data refresh  
  
Which connectivity mode should you use for the dataset?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DirectQuery mode

choices.label: B
choices.text: import mode

choices.label: C
choices.text: LiveConnect mode

choices.label: D
choices.text: push mode

definition.explanation:
Push datasets receive data pushed directly into Power BI by the source application via the REST API, so the report always shows the latest values instantly with no scheduled refresh and no repeated querying of the source, minimizing load on it. DirectQuery, by contrast, must query the source every time a visual is rendered, which would increase load on a frequently updating streaming source rather than minimize it.

**Learn more:** [Real-time streaming in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-real-time-streaming)

You are building a Power BI model to analyze inventory.  
  
You load data into three tables named Date, Product, and Inventory. The Inventory table is related to the Date and Product tables by one-to-many relationships.  
  
Inventory data is captured every day without exception. The correct inventory quantity for a product in a month is its final recorded value for that month.  
  
You need to create a DAX measure that displays the correct inventory value when users analyze inventory by year, month, or date.  
  
How should you complete the measure?
definition.template:
Last Inventory Count =
{{function}} (
    SUM ( 'Inventory'[QuantityAvailable] ),
    {{date_function}} ( 'Date'[Date] )
)
definition.explanation:
`CALCULATE` reevaluates the inventory quantity with the date filter replaced by the date returned by `LASTDATE`. `LASTDATE('Date'[Date])` returns the final date in the current year, month, or date context; because inventory is recorded daily, its quantity is the required ending inventory value.

**Learn more:** [CALCULATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax) · [LASTDATE function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/lastdate-function-dax)

finalExplanation: `CALCULATE` reevaluates the inventory quantity with the date filter replaced by the date returned by `LASTDATE`. `LASTDATE('Date'[Date])` returns the final date in the current year, month, or date context; because inventory is recorded daily, its quantity is the required ending inventory value.

Query groups are organizational tools only and do not affect performance.

Query groups are organizational tools only and do not affect performance.

definition.stemRaw: After creating the profit and loss dataset, which four actions should be completed, in sequence, so business-unit analysts see the appropriate profit and loss data?

slots.answer: From Power BI Desktop, create four roles.
From Power BI Desktop, add a Table Filter DAX Expression to the roles.
From Power BI Desktop, publish the dataset to powerbi.com.

items: From powerbi.com, assign the analysts the Contributor role to the workspace.

From powerbi.com, add role members to the roles.
From Power BI Desktop, create four roles.
From Power BI Desktop, publish the dataset to powerbi.com.
definition.explanation:
Define the RLS roles and their DAX table filters in Power BI Desktop, then publish the semantic model. Assign users to those roles in the Power BI service after publication. You have a Power BI semantic model containing two tables named Sales and Forecast. Both tables have a date column.  
  
You need to create a calculated table that covers the date range in both tables.  
  
How should you complete the DAX expression?
definition.template: daterange = {{function}} ( {{sales_boundary}} (Sales, [Date]), {{forecast_boundary}} (Forecast, [Date]))
definition.explanation:
CALENDAR returns a contiguous table of dates between inclusive start and end dates. MINX returns the earliest Sales date, and MAXX returns the latest Forecast date, producing a date table that spans the Sales and Forecast ranges.

**Learn more:** [CALENDAR function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calendar-function-dax)

finalExplanation: CALENDAR returns a contiguous table of dates between inclusive start and end dates. MINX returns the earliest Sales date, and MAXX returns the latest Forecast date, producing a date table that spans the Sales and Forecast ranges.

- Year-over-year calculations for all measures  
  
Which four actions should you perform, in sequence?

slots.answer: Use the first row as headers.
Unpivot all the columns other than Measure.
Rename the Attribute column as Year.
Change the data type of the Year column to Date.

items: Use headers as the first row.
Rename the Measure column as Year.
Rename the Attribute column as Year.
Use the first row as headers.
Unpivot all the columns other than Measure.
Change the data type of the Year column to Date.
definition.explanation: Promoting the first row establishes Measure and the individual years as column names. Unpivoting the year columns produces one row per measure-year value, which supports time-based visuals and calculations. The generated Attribute field holds the year values, so it is renamed to Year and converted to Date for time intelligence.

You have a Power BI report for the marketing department that reports on web traffic to a blog and includes data from the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730096957-8d3agih4.jpg)  
  
There is a one-to-many relationship from **Posts** to **Traffic** using the **URL** and **URL Visited** columns. The report includes the visuals shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730099858-aod421d7.png)  
  
The dataset requires a long time to refresh.  
  
You need to modify the **Posts** and **Traffic** queries to reduce load times.  
  
Which two actions will reduce the load times? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:**  
  
Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove the rows in Posts in which Posts[Publish Date] is in the last seven days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the rows in Traffic in which Traffic[URL Visited] does not contain ג€blogג€.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove Traffic[IP Address], Traffic[Browser Agent], and Traffic[Referring URL].

You manage a Power BI workspace containing a supplier quality dashboard. The dashboard includes 10 card visuals, two map visuals, and five bar chart visuals.  
  
The dashboard's mobile layout is shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783731094230-3besg23s.jpg)  
  
You need to change the dashboard mobile layout to meet these requirements:  
  
- Show only single-value visuals.  
- Minimize scrolling.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease the size of the card visuals. Remove the map and bar chart visuals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease the size of the map and bar chart visuals. Move all the card visuals to the top of the layout.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove the card visuals. Increase the size of the map and bar chart visuals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Move the bar chart visuals to the top of the layout. Remove the map visuals. Decrease the size of the card visuals.

definition.explanation:
Card visuals display individual values, whereas map and bar chart visuals display multiple data points. Removing the map and bar chart visuals ensures that only single-value visuals remain; decreasing the sizes of the remaining cards reduces the vertical mobile layout and therefore scrolling. Power BI dashboard phone layouts support resizing and unpinning tiles.

**Learn more:** [Optimize a dashboard for mobile phones - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-za/power-bi/create-reports/service-create-dashboard-mobile-phone-view)

finalExplanation: Card visuals display individual values, whereas map and bar chart visuals display multiple data points. Removing the map and bar chart visuals ensures that only single-value visuals remain; decreasing the sizes of the remaining cards reduces the vertical mobile layout and therefore scrolling. Power BI dashboard phone layouts support resizing and unpinning tiles.
